ch6-camera-bg.outcome: If your camera is already on, the effect applies immediately on your live feed. If your camera is off, the choice is saved and applied automatically the next time you turn the camera on — and it survives reloads.

host.html: There is no host control to force or clear anyone’s camera background. It is each participant’s own per-browser choice; a host cannot blur you for you.

ch6-camera-bg.note: Background effects run only on desktop browsers. On a phone or tablet the whole section is disabled and shows the note “Background effects are only supported on desktop”. Switch to a laptop or desktop if you need a virtual background.
ch6-camera-bg.figcap: Account settings → Preferences, showing the Change / blur background controls.

ch6-bg-states.heading: Every camera-background state

tiles.cap: The raw camera — your real room is shown. The default.
A gentle blur — the room is still readable behind you.
A stronger blur — shapes only, details lost.
Maximum blur — the room is fully obscured.
Scene replacement — you appear in front of the chosen image.
On phone/tablet web the section is greyed out with the desktop-only note.

ch6-bg-states.useWhen: Use a Blur level when you just want to hide a messy or private room while keeping a natural look; use a scene when you want a consistent, on-brand backdrop. Start with Light or Medium — Strong can look heavy on a busy room.

ch6-quality.heading: Video quality ceiling
rows: Rides the admin-allowed cap and lets the network adapt below it. The default.
Caps your outgoing camera at the lowest tier — kindest to a weak connection and CPU.
A middle ground between sharpness and bandwidth.
The crispest outgoing feed — best on a strong connection.
ch6-quality.note: Find this under Account settings → Preferences → Video quality. Its hint reads “Adapts to your network; pick your own ceiling.” This is a ceiling, not a fixed level: Canvas M always adapts downward on a weak uplink, so picking High doesn’t guarantee High — it only permits it. Lowering it is the better lever when your video stutters. Like the others, it applies live if your camera is on, else on the next camera-on.

host.html: An administrator can set an org-wide cap on the maximum quality anyone may choose. When that cap is below High, the tiers above it are greyed out and a note appears: “Admin caps the max at {level}.” Auto always stays selectable — it simply rides whatever the cap is. A participant cannot raise quality past the admin cap.

ch6-trouble.heading: Backgrounds & quality troubleshooting

rows.sym: The camera-background section is greyed out
rows.cause: You’re on a phone or tablet — background effects are desktop-only.
rows.fix: Use a desktop or laptop browser; the note “Background effects are only supported on desktop” confirms this.

rows.sym: High / Medium quality is greyed out
rows.cause: An administrator lowered the org-wide quality cap below that tier.
rows.fix: Pick a tier at or below the cap, or Auto. The note “Admin caps the max at …” names the limit.

rows.sym: Upload fails with “Ảnh quá lớn, chọn ảnh khác”
rows.cause: Even after compression the image won’t fit this browser’s storage (storage is nearly full).
rows.fix: Choose a smaller image, or clear space; presets and gradients always work.

rows.sym: Upload fails with “Không đọc được ảnh, chọn ảnh khác”
rows.cause: The chosen file isn’t a readable image.
rows.fix: Pick a standard image file (JPG/PNG/WebP).

rows.sym: My background / quality reset after signing in elsewhere
rows.cause: These are per-browser preferences, not synced to your account.
rows.fix: Re-pick them on the new device; the choice then sticks on that browser.

rows.sym: Camera background didn’t change while I was already on camera
rows.cause: Rarely the processor fails to swap mid-call; the picker never blocks on it.
rows.fix: Turn the camera off and on — the saved choice re-applies on the next camera-on.

ch6-trouble.note: If video stutters or freezes, lower Video quality first (try Low) before touching the background — it cuts both bandwidth and CPU, whereas a blur or scene adds a little CPU work.

legend.text: Hand (H) — the panning tool. Hold and drag to slide the canvas without selecting or drawing anything.
Selection (V or 1) — pick, move, and resize elements. The default tool. If you have the lasso preference on, this slot becomes Lasso selection instead.
Drawing shapes: Rectangle (R/2), Diamond (D/3), Ellipse (O/4), Arrow (A/5), Line (L/6).
Draw (P or X, also 7) — freehand pen. Text (T/8). Insert image (9).
Eraser (E/0) and Revision cloud (Q) — the dashed markup cloud for flagging changes.
Canvas M extras strip: the Stickers and Stamps pickers, the Ask MCM Bot tool, and the CAD view / 3D view openers — added next to the shape switcher.
Laser pointer (K) — a temporary dot for pointing during a walkthrough; reach it from More tools rather than the main strip.

ch7-tools.heading: The toolbar at a glance
rows: Drag the canvas around without touching elements.
Click to pick; drag to marquee-select; drag a handle to resize.
Click-drag a rectangle. Hold to keep drawing more.
Click a start point, click an end point. Snaps to nearby shapes.
Straight line; click again to add a bend, double-click to finish.
Click to place a text cursor and type. Double-clicking with Selection also starts text.
Pick an image file to drop on the canvas.
Drag over strokes to remove them.
Draw a dashed cloud to mark up a change.
A fading dot for pointing; lives under More tools.
ch7-tools.note: Number keys mirror the icons left to right (<kbd>1</kbd>–<kbd>0</kbd>). The same shortcuts work whether you are a host or a participant — the toolbar is identical for everyone with edit access.

ch7-extras.heading: The buttons beyond plain whiteboarding

tiles.cap: Two pickers labelled Stickers and Stamps. Open one, and a grid of assets appears with the hint “Pick → scroll to resize → click to place.” An empty library reads “No Stickers in the library yet.”

The bot tool (Ask MCM Bot) drops a prompt box on the canvas. Type any request — “summarize the meeting, list decisions” — and the answer is written onto the canvas. It shows “🤖 Working…” while it thinks.
CAD view opens a DXF in a pane; 3D view opens an IFC model. If the library has none, the popover reads “No DXF files in the library yet.” / “No IFC models in the library yet.”

ch7-extras.useWhen: Reach for the extras when plain shapes aren't enough: stickers and stamps to react or approve, the bot to pull answers out of the transcript, and the CAD/3D openers to inspect drawings and models right on the board. They sit in one strip next to the shape switcher; on a narrow phone screen they collapse into a single row below the toolbar.

ch7-place.heading: Drop a sticker, stamp, or bot answer
steps: Click Stickers or Stamps in the extras strip to open the picker.
Click an asset. A translucent ghost now follows your pointer — you are in placing mode.
Scroll the wheel (or pinch) to resize the ghost before you commit.
Click once on the canvas to drop the asset at that point.
For the bot, click Ask MCM Bot, click the canvas, then type your request in the floating box and press Send.
ch7-place.outcome: The sticker, stamp, or bot answer lands on the canvas as a normal element that everyone in the room sees — you can then select, move, or resize it like any shape.
ch7-place.note: Placing mode works the same with a mouse, an Apple Pencil, a Surface Pen, or a finger. With a pen, the ghost sits beside the tip rather than under your hand.
ch7-place.figcap: Placing mode: a ghost preview tracks the pointer until you click to commit.

ch7-nav.heading: Zoom, reset, and the mini-map
steps: Find the navigation widget in the bottom-right corner of the canvas — it is always there.
Click + (Zoom in) or − (Zoom out). The buttons grey out at the maximum and minimum zoom.
Read the live zoom percentage in the middle; click it to Reset zoom (100%).
Click the map icon to toggle the mini-map — its tooltip flips between Show navigation map and Hide navigation map.
On the mini-map, click or drag to move the camera; the bright rectangle is your current view.
ch7-nav.outcome: You can reach any corner of a large board without a scroll wheel or trackpad gestures — useful on a tablet. Your mini-map open/closed choice is remembered on this device.
ch7-nav.note: Moving your own camera is local: it does not move anyone else's view, and following is separate — that is the participants panel's job, covered earlier.
ch7-nav.figcap: The corner widget: zoom buttons, a clickable percentage, and the toggleable mini-map.

ch7-mental.heading: One infinite board, shared live
ch7-mental.lead: The canvas is a single, endless sheet that everyone in the room shares in real time. There are no pages and no edges — you pan and zoom to wherever the work is, and what you draw appears for everyone the instant you draw it.
ch7-mental.body: Two ideas keep it calm. First, your camera is yours: zooming or panning only moves your own view, never anyone else's, so you can wander off to inspect a detail without dragging the room with you. Second, your edits are everyone's: a shape, sticker, or bot answer you place is collaborative the moment it lands. The mini-map exists to reconcile the two — it shows the whole board at once so you never lose your bearings.
ch7-mental.pull: Your camera is yours; your edits are everyone's.

note.html: When a meeting has finished, the canvas switches to review mode and the editing extras step back — the Stickers, Stamps, and bot buttons disappear, while the CAD and 3D openers and the navigation widget stay so you can still inspect and move around.

ch7-trouble.heading: Canvas snags and fixes

rows.sym: The zoom + or − button is greyed out.
rows.cause: You're already at the maximum or minimum zoom.
rows.fix: Click the percentage to reset to 100%, or use the other button.

rows.sym: A sticker picker grid is empty.
rows.cause: No assets are bundled for that kind yet.
rows.fix: You'll see “No Stickers in the library yet” — use a stamp or a shape instead.

rows.sym: CAD view / 3D view opens an empty popover.
rows.cause: No DXF or IFC files have been uploaded to the room.
rows.fix: Add a file via the library bar on the right first, then re-open the view.

rows.sym: The Stickers, Stamps, and bot buttons vanished.
rows.cause: The meeting has finished — the canvas is read-only.
rows.fix: This is expected. You can still pan, zoom, and open CAD/3D views to review.

rows.sym: The bot says it can't answer.
rows.cause: A connection or API problem.
rows.fix: You'll see “The bot hit an error, try again.” — wait a moment and resend.

ch7-trouble.note: Most canvas controls are local-only, so a hiccup rarely affects the rest of the room — a quick retry or a zoom reset usually clears it.

ch8-where.heading: Where the decoration tools live
ch8-where.lead: Canvas M adds its decoration controls straight into the Excalidraw toolbar, sitting next to the shape buttons rather than in a separate panel. Look for the small strip of extra buttons: a Stickers button (a colourful character icon), a Stamps button, and a people-shaped Show authors toggle.
ch8-where.body: These three buttons share one host strip, so on a narrow screen they stay grouped as a single horizontal row instead of stacking into full-width buttons. The revision-cloud tool is different: it is a regular drawing tool in the main shape row, reachable with the keyboard shortcut <kbd>Q</kbd>.

note.html: Decoration tools that create canvas content — stickers, stamps, the bot, and text translation — are hidden when you open a finished meeting in review mode. A completed meeting is immutable and extract-only, so the buttons simply do not appear. The Show authors toggle stays available so you can still see who wrote what.

ch8-stickers.heading: Drop a sticker on the canvas
steps: Click the Stickers button in the toolbar. A popover opens showing a grid of chibi-animal stickers.
Read the hint at the top of the popover: Pick → scroll to resize → click to place.
Click any sticker tile. The popover closes and a translucent ghost of the sticker starts following your pointer.
Move over the canvas — the ghost previews the exact size and shows a live width × height readout.
Scroll the mouse wheel to resize before you commit (scroll up = bigger, down = smaller).
Click once on the canvas to drop the sticker at that point.
Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> at any time to cancel placing mode without dropping anything.
ch8-stickers.outcome: The sticker lands centred on your click and becomes a normal image element — free-floating, selectable, movable, and synced to everyone in the room.
ch8-stickers.note: Stickers and stamps work with a mouse, a trackpad, an Apple Pencil, a Surface Pen, or a touch finger — placing mode is built on pointer events, so all input types behave the same. With a pen, the ghost preview is offset slightly so it sits next to the stylus tip instead of under your hand.
ch8-stickers.figcap: The Stickers popover: a 16-tile grid of animal stickers with the pick-scroll-place hint.

ch8-sizing.heading: Sizing the ghost before you click

tiles.cap: Scroll down to shrink. The smallest the wheel allows is 12% of the base size.
Every pick starts at 100%. Base size is capped at 240px on the longest edge.
Scroll up to grow, up to 6× the base size. The readout updates as you scroll.

ch8-sizing.useWhen: The ghost is true WYSIWYG: it is drawn at the on-canvas scene size multiplied by your current zoom, so the floating preview is exactly what lands when you click. The corner readout (e.g. 180 × 180) is the scene size in canvas pixels, not screen pixels.

ch8-stamps.heading: Stamp an image so the mark travels with it
steps: Click the Stamps button. A popover opens with a 12-tile grid of postal-style stamps.
Click a stamp tile, then scroll to size and click on the canvas — exactly like a sticker.
To attach a stamp to an image, drop it directly on top of that image.
Drag the underlying image afterwards — the stamp moves with it.
ch8-stamps.outcome: A stamp dropped on top of an image adheres to it: the two are grouped, so dragging, selecting, or copying one carries the other. It behaves like a real rubber stamp on a photo. A stamp dropped on empty canvas stays free-floating, just like a sticker.
ch8-stamps.note: The topmost image under your click wins the binding. Canvas M skips its own anchor images (PDF and DXF views own their navigation toolbars) and skips other stamps — stamping a stamp does nothing, since you would just delete the old one. To detach a stamp later, select the group and use Excalidraw's Ungroup.
ch8-stamps.figcap: The Stamps popover: postal-style chibi-animal stamps with the same placing flow as stickers.

ch8-revcloud.heading: Cloud an area and attach a note
steps: Pick the revision-cloud tool from the shape row, or press <kbd>Q</kbd>.
Drag a rectangle over the area you want to flag. On release, the rectangle becomes a scalloped cloud outline.
A toast appears: Click where you want to place the note.
Click anywhere on the canvas. A text note reading Note drops at that spot.
An arrow is drawn from the note to the nearest scallop of the cloud, and all three pieces are grouped together.
Double-click the Note text to edit it; the arrow stays tethered as you move the note.
ch8-revcloud.outcome: You get a grouped revision marker — cloud, note, and connecting arrow — inherited from the colour, stroke width, roughness, and opacity that were active when you drew. Everything is synced to the room as standard canvas elements.
ch8-revcloud.note: A single click (no drag) leaves nothing behind — the placeholder is dropped silently. The note inherits your current font so typed text, including Vietnamese, renders correctly. The cloud, the arrow, and the note are all selected together right after creation, so you can move the whole marker as a unit immediately.
ch8-revcloud.figcap: A revision cloud with its arrow-tethered Note over a flagged region of the canvas.

ch8-authors.heading: See who wrote each piece of text
ch8-authors.lead: Canvas M stamps the creator's name onto every text element they add. An author badge — a small avatar plus a short name — floats above the top-left corner of authored text so you can tell at a glance who left it.
ch8-authors.body: By default badges are quiet: one appears only over the text you have selected or are hovering. To reveal every author at once, click the people-shaped Show authors button in the toolbar; its tooltip flips to Hide authors while active. Click again to go back to the calm, selection-only view. Badges are deliberately text-only — shapes, images, stickers, and stamps don't get them, which keeps the canvas readable.
ch8-authors.pull: Bot answers carry a fixed identity: a 🤖 avatar and the MCM Bot name, so AI-generated text is always distinguishable from a person's.

note.html: A badge survives its author leaving the room — the name is snapshotted onto the element, so it keeps showing even after that person disconnects. If a name can't be resolved, the badge falls back to Guest. Badges never appear on text bound inside a container (like the bot frame's own label), because the frame already shows who it belongs to.

ch8-ref.heading: Decoration tools at a glance
rows: Image, grouped to the image beneath it
ch8-ref.note: Placing-mode controls are identical for stickers and stamps: scroll resizes (0.12× to 6×), click places, Esc cancels. The wheel resizes the decoration instead of zooming the canvas while a ghost is active.

ch8-trouble.heading: When decorations don't behave

rows.sym: The Stickers / Stamps buttons aren't in the toolbar
rows.cause: You're viewing a finished meeting in review mode, where content-creating tools are hidden.
rows.fix: Open the live meeting instead — review canvases are immutable and extract-only.

rows.sym: I picked a sticker but nothing follows my pointer
rows.cause: The asset failed to load (missing or forbidden file); placing mode never started.
rows.fix: Pick a different tile. A failed asset is skipped quietly without an error popup.

rows.sym: Clicking off the canvas dropped nothing
rows.cause: A click outside the canvas bounds cancels placing instead of placing the decoration.
rows.fix: Aim your click inside the canvas area. Press the tool again to retry.

rows.sym: The wheel won't zoom the canvas
rows.cause: A sticker or stamp ghost is active — the wheel resizes the decoration, not the view.
rows.fix: Click to place, or press ⌫Esc to cancel, then the wheel zooms normally.

rows.sym: My stamp didn't stick to the image
rows.cause: It landed on empty canvas, on an MCM anchor (PDF/DXF), or on another stamp — none of which bind.
rows.fix: Drop the stamp squarely on top of the target image element.

rows.sym: The revision-cloud drag did nothing
rows.cause: The drag was too small — a cloud needs at least a 12px-by-12px rectangle.
rows.fix: Drag a larger area, then click to place the note when prompted.

rows.sym: A badge shows “Guest” instead of a name
rows.cause: The author's identity couldn't be resolved from the stamped name or profile cache.
rows.fix: Expected for anonymous or departed peers — the marker is still correct.

ch8-trouble.note: Stickers and stamps ride the same upload pipeline as a pasted image, so they survive a late-join and a reopen. If a peer momentarily sees an empty box, it resolves once the bytes finish syncing.

ch9-translate-concept.heading: A translation is a real element, not a tooltip
ch9-translate-concept.lead: Canvas M does not show you a private, hover-only translation. When you translate a text element, it creates a new child text element placed just below the original. Because it is a genuine canvas element, it rides the normal collaboration pipeline — every peer in the room sees the same translated line, with no extra setup.
ch9-translate-concept.body: The child stays linked to its source. Move or resize the original and the translation follows by the same offset, keeping the pair together. Delete the original and its translations are swept away with it. The translation is drawn in a muted grey so it reads as secondary text beneath the source.
ch9-translate-concept.pull: Translate once, and the whole room reads it — the result is a shared canvas line, not a personal pop-up.

diagram.label: Source text → linked translation child
diagram.cap: Picking a language adds a grey, linked line directly under the original.

note.html: The three languages share one round-trip. Picking Tiếng Việt also warms the cache for English and 한국어, so your next language choice on the same text is instant.

ch9-translate-steps.heading: Turn a note into another language
steps: Click a single text element on the canvas to select it. The pill appears only when exactly one item is selected.
A small Translate pill floats just above the text's top-left corner. It carries a language icon and follows the text as you pan or zoom.
Click Translate to translate into your current app language straight away — its tooltip reads Translate to {lang} for whichever language that is.
To pick a different target, click the ▾ caret (tooltip Choose another language) and choose 🇻🇳 Tiếng Việt, 🇬🇧 English or 🇰🇷 한국어.
The button shows Translating… while it works, then a grey translated line appears below your text.
ch9-translate-steps.outcome: The translated line sits under the source, visible to everyone in the room. Translate again into a second language and the new line stacks neatly below the first.
ch9-translate-steps.note: Pick the same language twice and Canvas M rewrites the existing line in place — it never piles up duplicate translations of the same pair.
ch9-translate-steps.figcap: The Translate pill anchored above a selected text note.

ch9-translate-states.heading: Every face of the Translate pill

tiles.cap: Default. The Translate label plus a ▾ caret. Clicking the label uses your app language; the caret opens the three-language menu.
While the request is in flight the label reads Translating… and every button is disabled so you can't fire a second call.
Shown after you edit the source. A refresh icon and the label Refresh translation replace the normal pill; the stale lines fade to signal they're out of date.

ch9-translate-states.useWhen: Watch the pill swap to Refresh translation whenever you change the source text after translating — that's your cue the lines below no longer match.

ch9-translate-ref.heading: Translate controls and behaviours
rows: Translates into your current app language in one click.
Names the target language the one-click button will use.
Opens the menu: Tiếng Việt, English, 한국어.
Shown on the button during the request; all buttons disabled.
Re-translates every out-of-date line against the edited source.
Translation is out of date — click to refresh
Explains why the pill changed to the refresh state.
The pill's aria-label for screen readers.
ch9-translate-ref.note: If the translation provider is unavailable, or returns the same text it was given, no line is added — the canvas is left untouched rather than cluttered with a duplicate.

host.html: There is no host-side switch for the on-canvas Translate pill — any participant who selects a text element can use it. (The separate chat translation toggle lives in the AI Tools panel; see the chat chapter.)

ch9-bot-steps.heading: Drop the bot and ask a question
steps: In the toolbar, click the bot icon (tooltip Ask MCM Bot). The pointer enters placing mode and a small bot ghost follows your cursor.
Click anywhere on the canvas to drop it. Click outside the canvas, or press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, to cancel placing.
A small prompt box opens at the drop point, with the placeholder Type your request… (e.g. summarize the meeting, list decisions).
Type any request — summarise, list decisions, translate this, and so on — then click Send or press Enter. Use Shift+Enter for a new line, Esc or × to cancel.
A framed panel reading 🤖 Working… appears at the drop point, then is replaced in place by the bot's answer.
ch9-bot-steps.outcome: The answer lands as a dark, cyan-bordered 🤖 MCM BOT panel — a normal, movable canvas element everyone in the room can see and reposition.
ch9-bot-steps.note: Nothing fires automatically. The bot only runs on your explicit click, so there's no risk of two people triggering it at once — the prompt box is local to you; only the answer panel is shared.

host.html: Any participant can drop the bot — there is no host gate in the tool itself. Access is checked server-side by room membership, so only people actually in the meeting can run it.

ch9-bot-steps.figcap: The bot prompt box open at a drop point on the canvas.

legend.text: Bot header — every answer panel opens with 🤖 MCM BOT in monospace so it's unmistakably the bot's, not a peer's note.
Answer body — light text on a dark panel, wrapped to the frame width. This is what the bot wrote in reply to your request.
Cyan frame — the panel is a real rectangle with bound text. Drag it, resize it, or delete it like any element; changes sync to the room.
Authored by MCM Bot — the panel is stamped with the bot's identity, so it's excluded from the meeting context the bot reads next time (it never quotes its own answers back to you).

ch9-trouble.heading: When translate or the bot misbehaves

rows.sym: No Translate pill appears
rows.cause: Nothing selected, more than one element selected, or you selected a translation line rather than a source.
rows.fix: Click a single text element. Translating a translation is blocked on purpose, so the pill hides on those grey lines.

rows.sym: Pill shows Refresh translation, not Translate
rows.cause: You edited the source text after translating, so the lines below it are now stale and faded.
rows.fix: Click Refresh translation to re-translate every out-of-date line in one pass.

rows.sym: Clicking a language adds nothing
rows.cause: The source is empty/whitespace, or the provider is unavailable and returned the original text.
rows.fix: Make sure the note has real text. If the provider is down, Canvas M intentionally adds no line; try again later.

rows.sym: Translation moved when I dragged the note
rows.cause: Expected. Translation lines are linked to their source and shift by the same offset to stay together.
rows.fix: Nothing to fix — move the source and the pair travels as one. Delete the source to remove its translations too.

rows.sym: Bot panel says "The bot hit an error, try again."
rows.cause: The request to the bot failed or the server returned an error.
rows.fix: Press the bot icon again, drop a fresh prompt, and resend. The error text replaces the loading frame in place.

rows.sym: Dropped the bot but no prompt box
rows.cause: You clicked outside the canvas area, which cancels placing.
rows.fix: Re-arm the bot from the toolbar and click inside the canvas to drop it.

ch9-trouble.note: The bot reads the meeting's chat, voice transcript, canvas notes (with authors), participants and shelf files as context — but it skips its own previous answers, so it won't loop on "no info" replies.

ch10-model.heading: One screen, shared to everyone
ch10-model.lead: Screen sharing in Canvas M is deliberately simple: at any moment one person in the room can present their screen, and everyone else watches it live. There is no "request to present" queue and no host approval step — whoever clicks Present first holds the floor until they stop.
ch10-model.body: Your screen travels over a separate live-media channel, not the drawing canvas. That means the canvas, chat, and captions keep working normally while a share is running. As a viewer you don't have to do anything to start watching — the moment a presenter begins, a floating viewer appears for you automatically. When the presenter stops (or leaves the room), the viewer disappears on its own.
ch10-model.pull: Whoever clicks Present first holds the floor. There is no queue and no host approval.

diagram.label: Presenter → live channel → every viewer
diagram.cap: The presenter's screen is sent over a dedicated media channel. Viewers join silently — no camera or microphone prompt — purely to receive the screen.

note.html: Because only one person can present at a time, your Present button is disabled while someone else is presenting. Wait for them to finish, then it unlocks.

ch10-present.heading: Share your screen
steps: Find the Present button in the meeting header — it sits in the media group beside the microphone and camera controls, drawn as a monitor-with-arrow icon. Hover it to confirm the Present tooltip.
Click Present. Your browser opens its own picker asking which entire screen, window, or browser tab you want to share.
Choose a source and confirm in the browser dialog. Sharing begins the instant the real screen feed starts — not when you click, so cancelling the picker leaves nothing shared.
Watch the Present button take on its active (highlighted) state. That is your confirmation you are now the presenter; you keep seeing your own screen, so no extra viewer window opens for you.
When you're done, click the highlighted Present button again to stop. The share ends immediately and everyone's viewer closes.
ch10-present.outcome: You are presenting. Every other participant sees your screen in a floating viewer, and a small screen badge appears on your tile in the participants bar.
ch10-present.note: Cancelling the browser's screen picker is harmless — nothing is broadcast and the button returns to its normal state. Presence is only announced once the live feed actually starts.

host.html: There is no host "give me the screen" or "stop their share" control. Sharing is self-service and governed only by the single-share lock — a host who wants to present simply waits for the current presenter to stop.

ch10-states.heading: Every state of the Present button

tiles.cap: Default. The monitor icon with the Present tooltip. Click to open the screen picker.
Highlighted/active. You are the current presenter. Click again to stop sharing.
Disabled. Another participant is presenting (single-share lock). It re-enables the moment they stop.
Disabled, with the tip "Screen sharing isn't supported on this device or browser (e.g. iPad / iPhone). Present from a computer instead."
Disabled. You're reviewing a finished meeting — live sharing is switched off entirely in read-only review.
While you present, a 📺 badge labelled "Sharing screen" sits on your avatar in the participants bar.

ch10-states.useWhen: If the button looks greyed out, check these states in order: are you in a finished-meeting review, is someone else already presenting, or is your device simply unable to share?

ch10-popout.heading: Pop the share into its own window
ch10-popout.lead: The ⧉ button — tooltip "Open in a separate window to drag to another screen" — lifts the live screen out of the in-app viewer and into a standalone, always-on-top window you can drag onto a second monitor. The drawing canvas keeps the rest of your first screen to yourself.
ch10-popout.body: While popped out, the in-app viewer shows the note "Watching in a separate window" in place of the picture, and live captions travel with the share into the pop-out window. Closing the pop-out window — or clicking back in the app — returns the picture to the in-app viewer and brings the captions home. The viewer also re-homes itself automatically if the presenter stops while you're popped out.

note.html: Pop out uses the browser's Document Picture-in-Picture feature, which today is Chromium-only (Chrome, Edge, and similar). On Firefox and Safari the ⧉ button simply doesn't appear, and the in-app viewer remains your way to watch.

diagram.label: In-app viewer → pop-out window on monitor 2
diagram.cap: Pop out moves the live video into its own OS window without re-loading the feed, so the picture never flickers as it leaves the app.

ch10-audio.heading: Hearing a shared tab or system sound
ch10-audio.lead: If a presenter chose to include audio when picking a tab or screen — for example to play a video clip — Canvas M plays that shared sound to you automatically alongside the picture.
ch10-audio.body: Browsers sometimes block audio from starting until you've interacted with the page. If a share's sound doesn't come through at first, simply click anywhere in the app (or press any key); the audio resumes on that first gesture. Shared audio is separate from the meeting's voice call — muting yourself or others in the call has no effect on a presenter's shared tab sound.

note.html: Sharing system or tab audio is a choice you make in your browser's screen-picker dialog (e.g. a "Share tab audio" checkbox), not in Canvas M. If viewers can't hear your clip, re-share and tick that box.

ch10-ref.heading: Screen-sharing controls at a glance
rows: Starts your screen share; click again while active to stop. Locked while another person presents.
Indicates you are the current presenter.
Your tile in the participants bar
Shows everyone who is currently presenting.
Names the presenter you're watching, with a live dot.
Moves the live screen into a separate, draggable window.
Collapses the viewer to its title bar, or restores the picture.
Shown while the share is popped out to another window.
ch10-ref.note: Labels are quoted exactly as they appear in the English interface. The presenter never sees a viewer pane — they watch their own screen directly.

host.html: None of these are host controls. There is no moderator screen-share lock, force-stop, or approval step — the single-share lock is fully automatic.

ch10-trouble.heading: When sharing misbehaves

rows.sym: Present button is greyed out
rows.cause: Someone else is already presenting (single-share lock), you're in a finished-meeting review, or your device can't share.
rows.fix: Wait for the current presenter to stop, exit review mode, or present from a computer if the tip says it's unsupported.

rows.sym: Tooltip says screen sharing isn't supported
rows.cause: Your browser has no screen-capture API — typically iPad / iPhone Safari.
rows.fix: Present from a desktop or laptop browser instead, as the tip advises.

rows.sym: Toast: "Couldn't present your screen."
rows.cause: The share failed to start — connection or media error (any detail appears after the message).
rows.fix: Click Present again to retry; check your network if it persists.

rows.sym: Clicked Present but nothing shared
rows.cause: You cancelled the browser's screen-picker dialog. Sharing only begins when a source is confirmed.
rows.fix: Click Present again and pick a screen, window, or tab.

rows.sym: Viewer froze or went black
rows.cause: The presenter minimised the shared window, so its picture paused.
rows.fix: No action needed — it recovers automatically when they bring the window back.

rows.sym: No sound from a shared clip
rows.cause: The browser blocked audio until you interact, or the presenter didn't share audio.
rows.fix: Click anywhere in the app to resume audio; ask the presenter to re-share with tab audio on.

rows.sym: No Pop out button in the viewer
rows.cause: Your browser doesn't support Document Picture-in-Picture (Firefox / Safari).
rows.fix: Use the in-app viewer; minimise it to free up the canvas.

rows.sym: Joined mid-share and see nothing
rows.cause: A late joiner is reconciled against the live share automatically.
rows.fix: The viewer should appear within moments; refresh the page if it doesn't.

ch10-trouble.note: The error toast and the disabled-button tip are the only on-screen messages screen sharing surfaces; everything else recovers silently.

ch11-model.heading: One shelf, shared by everyone
ch11-model.lead: The library is the room's shared shelf of files. Anything you upload appears for every participant, and anything they upload appears for you. It is not your personal storage — it belongs to this meeting.
ch11-model.body: Four kinds of file are first-class here: ordinary images, DXF CAD drawings, PDF documents, and IFC 3D building models. Each tile carries a small type badge — IMG, DXF, PDF, IFC, or FILE for anything else. A file in the library is just a file; it does nothing until you place it on the canvas by clicking or dragging its tile.
ch11-model.pull: Adding a file to the library shares it with the whole room. Placing it on the canvas is a separate, second step.

diagram.label: Upload → shelf → canvas
diagram.cap: A file flows from your device into the shared shelf, then onto the canvas only when you click or drag it.

note.html: When you paste or drop an image straight onto the canvas, Canvas M quietly adds it to the library too, so peers receive it. App-generated assets — stickers, stamps, and the snapshot images behind PDF, DXF and IFC anchors — are deliberately kept out of the shelf so it stays clean.

ch11-upload.heading: Upload from your device
steps: Open the library panel in the meeting.
Click + Upload image / DXF / PDF / IFC · or drag & drop at the top of the panel.
Pick one or more files — the picker accepts images, <kbd>.dxf</kbd>, <kbd>.pdf</kbd> and <kbd>.ifc</kbd>. You can select several at once.
Alternatively, drag files from your desktop straight onto the panel; the button changes to Drop files to upload while you hover.
Wait for the tile to appear — IFC models are baked in the background and can take several seconds for large files.
ch11-upload.outcome: Each accepted file becomes a tile in the shelf, tagged with your name as the uploader, and is shared with everyone in the room.
ch11-upload.note: Only images, DXF, PDF and IFC are accepted. Drop anything else and you get “Only images, DXF, PDF and IFC are supported for now. Skipped: name”, and that one file is skipped while the rest carry on.
ch11-upload.figcap: The library panel with the upload button and the My Files shelf entry.

ch11-shelf.heading: Reuse a file from “My Files”
steps: Click From my shelf (the folder-heart button next to Upload).
The My Files picker opens with the hint Click to copy into this meeting.
Click any row to copy that document into the meeting; its row shows Copying into the meeting… while it works.
If the file is marked Private, confirm the prompt that warns everyone in the meeting will be able to see it.
The picker closes and the copied file appears as a normal library tile, owned by you.
ch11-shelf.outcome: The meeting gets its own private copy of the document — baked and encrypted for this room. Deleting it here never touches the original on your shelf.

host.html: From my shelf only appears for internal accounts. If you do not see it, your account simply isn't connected to a personal shelf — use the upload button instead; the result is identical.

ch11-shelf.note: Each row shows the file kind, name, a Private or Sharable badge, and its size. If your shelf is empty you'll read “Your shelf is empty — upload from the home page, under “My Files”.”

ch11-toolbar.heading: Search, filter, sort and view
rows: Filters tiles by file name or uploader
Placeholder reads “Search by name or uploader…”; matching is live as you type
Each chip shows a count; chips with zero files are hidden, but All always shows
Shows tiles as rows with a relative timestamp
Times read “just now”, “2m”, “3h”, “5d”, then a date
Groups files under collapsible type headings
Sections: CAD drawings, IFC models, PDF documents, Images, Other files — click a heading to collapse it
ch11-toolbar.note: The search box, chips, sort and view controls only appear once the room has at least one file. None of these settings are saved — each time you open the meeting the library starts on Newest, grid view, All files.

ch11-states.heading: The three resting states

tiles.cap: “No files in this room yet.” with the hint “Drag images here or paste/drop onto the canvas to get started.” The toolbar controls stay hidden.
“No files match the filters.” with a Clear filters button that resets the search box and the chip back to All.
After the meeting ends the upload button is disabled with the tooltip “The meeting has finished — the library is read-only, uploads are disabled.” You can still place existing files on the canvas.

ch11-states.useWhen: Use these to tell apart “nothing here yet” from “your filter hid everything” — the first means upload something, the second means clear your filters.

ch11-lock.heading: Locking, deleting, and linking
ch11-lock.lead: Each tile carries three actions. Hover a tile to reveal them: a link button (🔗), a lock toggle (🔓 unlocked, 🔒 locked), and a delete button (✕).
ch11-lock.body: Lock a file to stop anyone else removing it. Once locked, only the person who locked it or the original uploader can unlock it again — anyone else trying gets “Only locker (who locked it) or uploader (the uploader) can unlock it.” Delete removes the file from the library and every copy of it on the canvas, for everyone, after a confirmation. If the file is locked by someone else the delete button is disabled and reads “File is locked by name”; click it anyway and you're told to ask them to unlock it first. The link button connects the file to a text element you've selected on the canvas, so the file can be mentioned from there.
ch11-lock.pull: Locking protects a file from deletion; it does not stop people placing it on the canvas.

note.html: Deleting a file is destructive and shared — it pulls every on-canvas copy out from under every participant. The confirmation spells this out: “Every image using this file on the canvas is removed too (for everyone).” There is no undo from the library.

ch11-trouble.heading: Library troubleshooting

rows.sym: My file was skipped on upload
rows.cause: The type isn't supported — only images, DXF, PDF and IFC are accepted
rows.fix: Convert it or upload a supported format; you'll see “…Skipped: name” for each rejected file

rows.sym: “Couldn't process IFC file”
rows.cause: The IFC model failed to bake (corrupt or unsupported geometry)
rows.fix: Re-export the IFC from your authoring tool and try again; other files in the same batch are unaffected

rows.sym: The upload button is greyed out
rows.cause: The meeting has finished — the library is read-only
rows.fix: You can still drag existing files onto the canvas; uploading needs a live meeting

rows.sym: Clicking a tile doesn't add a second copy
rows.cause: That file is already on the canvas; Canvas M scrolls to it instead
rows.fix: This is intended — drag the tile if you genuinely want it in a new spot

rows.sym: I can't delete a file
rows.cause: It's locked by someone else
rows.fix: Ask the person who locked it, or the original uploader, to unlock or delete it

rows.sym: Search controls are missing
rows.cause: The room has no files yet
rows.fix: Upload or drop a file — the toolbar appears once there's at least one

ch11-trouble.note: Search and filter settings reset every time you reopen the meeting — that is by design, not a fault.

ch12-mental-model.eyebrow: How documents live on the canvas
ch12-mental-model.heading: Anchors, panes, and what your peers see
ch12-mental-model.lead: Every document you open started life as an upload in the room library — the bar on the right where files are grouped under PDF documents, CAD drawings, and IFC models. Dropping one onto the canvas creates an anchor: a tile that shows the document in place, sized and positioned like any other element.
ch12-mental-model.body: There are two ways to look at a document, and they behave differently. A PDF shows its page directly on the canvas inside the anchor — you read it where it sits. A DXF drawing or an IFC model can also be opened in a dedicated pane that docks to the right edge of the screen, giving you a full interactive viewer with its own toolbar. The canvas anchor is the shared object; the pane is your personal workspace for inspecting it.
ch12-mental-model.pull: The page you turn to is shared. The layers you toggle, the model you orbit, the slice you cut — those stay on your screen.

diagram.label: Library file → canvas anchor → docked viewer pane
diagram.cap: An uploaded file becomes a canvas anchor; DXF and IFC anchors can additionally open in a right-docked pane.

note.html: Canvas M accepts only four kinds of file. If someone tries to add anything else, the room reports “Only images, DXF, PDF and IFC are supported for now.” and skips it.

ch12-pdf-pages.heading: Read a PDF and turn its pages
steps: Find the PDF anchor on the canvas — it carries a 📄 label with the file name and, once loaded, a page counter like 3 / 24.
To change the page, right-click the anchor. A small menu appears with Edit PDF (change page) and Cancel.
Choose Edit PDF (change page) to drop the anchor into focus mode. A toolbar appears across the bottom of the tile.
Use ← (Previous page) and → (Next page) to move through the document; the indicator in the middle shows the current page and total.
When you are done, click × Exit or press Esc to leave focus mode.
ch12-pdf-pages.outcome: The page you land on is saved to the anchor and pushed to everyone in the room, so the whole meeting is looking at the same figure. The arrows grey out at the first and last page.
ch12-pdf-pages.note: Double-clicking a PDF anchor does nothing on purpose — it will not drop you into Excalidraw's text editor the way a plain rectangle would.

host.html: When you are reviewing a finished meeting in read-only mode, page changes are blocked — the anchor stays on whatever page the live meeting ended on.

ch12-pdf-pages.figcap: A PDF anchor in focus mode, showing the page navigation toolbar.

ch12-cad-open.heading: Open a DXF in the CAD view
steps: Click the CAD view button in the canvas toolbar (the floor-plan icon, tooltip “CAD view — open DXF in a pane”).
A popover titled DXF in library lists every drawing in the room. Pick one to open it as a tab in the right-docked pane.
Alternatively, right-click a DXF anchor on the canvas and choose Open in CAD view.
Each file opens in its own tab marked 📍; click a tab to switch, click its × to close just that drawing.
Drag the left edge of the pane (the resize handle) to make the viewer wider or narrower.
Close the whole pane with the × in the top-right corner.
ch12-cad-open.outcome: The DXF loads into an interactive viewer. Pan by dragging, zoom with the scroll wheel. Re-opening a drawing that is already a tab simply switches to it rather than duplicating.
ch12-cad-open.note: If the popover says “No DXF files in the library yet.” with the hint “Upload .dxf via the library bar on the right.”, there is simply nothing to open yet.
ch12-cad-open.figcap: A DXF open in the right-docked CAD view with the Layers, Fit, and Lock toolbar.

legend.text: Layers — opens the Layers ({count}) panel. Tick or untick each layer to show or hide it; the colour swatch matches the DXF layer colour. All turns everything on, None turns everything off.
Fit — resets the view to frame the whole drawing (tooltip “Fit DXF to pane (reset the view)”).
Lock / Locked — freezes pan and zoom so you cannot nudge the drawing by accident. Click again to unlock; the tooltip reads “View is locked — click to unlock pan/zoom” when active.
Tab strip — one tab per open drawing, each with a × to close it; the pane × at top-right closes the entire CAD view.

ch12-3d-open.heading: Open a building model in 3D view
steps: Click the 3D view button in the canvas toolbar (the cube icon, tooltip “3D view — open IFC model in a pane”).
The popover IFC in library lists every model; pick one to open it as a tab marked 🧊 in the right-docked pane.
Or right-click an IFC anchor on the canvas and choose Open in 3D view.
Once it loads, drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, and click any element to select it and open its properties.
Use Fit to reframe the whole model whenever you lose your bearings.
Resize the pane from its left edge, switch models via the tabs, and close with the tab × or the pane ×.
ch12-3d-open.outcome: Clicking an element opens a properties panel listing its Name, Type, Category, Family, and Type name, plus any extra Properties the model carries. Close it with its × (Deselect).
ch12-3d-open.note: While the model is still loading you will see “Loading 3D model…”. Every toolbar button stays greyed out until the model is ready.
ch12-3d-open.figcap: An IFC model open in 3D view with the storeys, objects, section, measure, and ghost toolbar.

legend.text: Fit — frames the whole model and resets the camera (“Fit model to pane”).
Storeys — lists the building's floors by elevation. Click one to isolate it; click All to show every storey again. The badge shows the floor count.

Objects — the object tree, grouped storey → category → element. Expand a branch, click an element to select and frame it, or use the eye toggle (👁 / 🚫) to hide and show it. Show all storeys clears any isolation.
View style — a three-way switch: Shaded, Clay, Wireframe (see the gallery below).

Section — the scissors group with X, Y, Z cut axes. Pick an axis, drag the plane in the 3D frame to slice; Flip swaps which half is kept, and the eye button hides or shows the cut plane while keeping the slice. Click the active axis again to turn the section off.
Measure — click two points on the model to read the distance; the result appears as 📏 with two decimals. Click Measure again to stop.
Ghost — fades everything except your current selection so a single element stands out.

ch12-3d-styles.heading: Three ways to render the model

tiles.cap: Shows each element's original colour — the realistic default.
Overrides everything with a uniform grey, so form reads without colour noise.
Shows edge lines only — useful for seeing through the model.

ch12-3d-styles.useWhen: Switch to Clay for clean massing discussions, Wireframe to inspect structure behind a facade, and back to Shaded when colour matters.

ch12-3d-reference.heading: Every 3D-view control at a glance
rows: Reframe the whole model and reset the camera
Fit model to pane (reset the view)
Isolate one floor; All shows every floor
Browse the storey / category / element tree; select, show, hide
Cut the model along an axis; drag the plane to move it
{axis}-axis section — drag the plane in the 3D frame to move it
Swap which half of the section is kept
Flip — swap which half is kept
Hide the cut plane but keep the slice
Hide the cut plane (keep the slice)
Click two points to read the distance
Measure distance — click 2 points on the model
Ghost — fade everything except the selection
ch12-3d-reference.note: Section, Flip, and the plane toggle stay disabled until you have picked a cut axis. While a section is active the hint “Drag the cut plane in the 3D frame to move it.” sits beside the toolbar.

ch12-trouble.heading: Document viewing — troubleshooting

rows.sym: A PDF / DXF / IFC tile shows “Waiting for … file from peer…”
rows.cause: The file bytes have not reached you yet — the person who added it is still syncing it across.
rows.fix: Wait a moment; it fills in automatically once the file arrives. No action needed.

rows.sym: “Maximum DXF files already open” (or “Maximum 3D models already open”)
rows.cause: Every viewer slot is in use — the renderer caps how many heavy models run at once.
rows.fix: Close another open file or tab, then try opening this one again.

rows.sym: “Couldn't read DXF: …” or “Couldn't read IFC model: …”
rows.cause: The file is corrupt or in an unsupported variant; the message after the colon is the underlying reason.
rows.fix: Ask the owner to re-export and re-upload the file.

rows.sym: A DXF tab shows “DXF file not found”
rows.cause: The tab is left over from a different meeting; its file is not in this room's library.
rows.fix: Close the phantom tab — Canvas M also prunes these automatically once the library loads.

rows.sym: The 3D toolbar buttons are all greyed out
rows.cause: The model is still loading (“Loading 3D model…”) or has no storeys / objects to show.
rows.fix: Wait for the model to finish; tooltips like “No storeys” / “No objects” mean that data simply isn't in the file.

rows.sym: Page turns on a PDF have no effect
rows.cause: You are reviewing a finished meeting in read-only mode, where page changes are blocked.
rows.fix: This is expected — read-only review keeps the page fixed.

ch12-trouble.note: Pan, zoom, and orbit happen inside the viewer pane only — they never move the underlying canvas, so you can explore freely without disturbing the shared layout.

legend.text: Header — the title Conversation on the left, and on the right the auto-translate toggle.
Auto-translate toggle — the globe button. Its tooltip reads Auto-translate (on) or Auto-translate (off) depending on state; it tints when active.

Message stream — messages grouped by author. The first message in a group carries the avatar, name and time; later messages from the same person within three minutes are bare bubbles indented beneath.
Your own messages — labelled You and styled distinctly from peers' bubbles.
Composer — a two-row card: a one-line text area on top that grows as you type, and an action row below.
Action row — left to right: the emoji (smiley) button, the Mention file / bot (@) button, the Attach image (paperclip) button, then the Send button on the right.

ch13-states.heading: When the panel is quiet

tiles.cap: Before you join a live collaboration the panel shows a chat icon, the title Start a live collaboration session, and the subtitle Messages are end-to-end encrypted with the room key. There is no composer yet.
In a live room with an empty history you see No messages yet and the hint Type @ to mention a file, @bot to ask AI. The composer is ready below.

Open a finished meeting for review and the history is visible but frozen. The composer is replaced by the notice Reviewing a finished meeting — chat is read-only. Reactions and replies are disabled too.

ch13-states.useWhen: Read these states as signals: an encryption subtitle means you haven't started collaborating yet; the read-only notice means the meeting is closed and extract-only.

ch13-mention.heading: Reference a file from the library
steps: Type @ anywhere in your draft, or click the Mention file / bot (@) button to insert one and open the picker.
Keep typing to filter — the picker lists up to eight matching library files by name, plus the MCM Bot option at the top.
Use <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd> to move the highlight, then <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd> to insert; or click an entry. Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to dismiss the picker.
The file is inserted as a coloured mention chip in your message.
In the sent message, click the mention chip — its tooltip reads Click to scroll to file on canvas — to fly the canvas to that image.
ch13-mention.outcome: Recipients see the same chip. Clicking it scrolls and zooms to the matching image on the canvas.
ch13-mention.note: If the picker finds nothing it shows No files in this room's library yet. when the library is empty, or No files match "…" with your query when none match. If you click a mention whose image isn't placed yet, an alert explains: This file isn't on the canvas yet. Open the library and click it to place first.

ch13-bot.heading: @bot — the in-chat assistant
ch13-bot.lead: Type @bot followed by a question to ask the room's AI assistant, MCM Bot. Pick it from the @ picker — labelled MCM Bot with the note Ask AI about the design / project — or just type @bot by hand.
ch13-bot.body: When you send a line containing @bot, your message posts as normal and the assistant starts working. A bot bubble with an animated three-dot thinking indicator appears while it composes. The bot reads context from the room — the last several chat lines, the full voice transcript so far, text written on the canvas, who is present, and the library file names — then replies in your preferred language. Its answer lands as a distinct robot-avatar bubble from MCM Bot.
ch13-bot.pull: Ask in plain language: @bot summarise the open questions or @bot what did we decide about the logo?

diagram.label: How @bot answers
diagram.cap: Your @bot line → thinking dots → MCM Bot gathers room context → reply bubble in your language.

note.html: If the assistant has nothing useful it replies Sorry, I couldn't answer. Try again later. If the connection or AI service fails it replies I can't reply right now (connection or API problem). Either way the thinking indicator clears.

ch13-react.heading: Tapback reactions and quoted replies
steps: Hover any message (your own or a peer's) to reveal a floating reaction bar above the bubble.
Click an emoji — the set is 👍 ❤️ 😂 😮 🎉 🔥 👀 🙏 💯 ✅ 🤔 😢 — to attach it. Clicking the same emoji again removes your reaction.
Reactions appear as a pill under the bubble with a running count; the tooltip reads {n} people. Your own reactions are highlighted.
To reply, click the curved-arrow Reply button at the right end of that same hover bar (tooltip Reply to this message).
A quote banner appears above the composer showing the author and a snippet; type your answer and send. Press Esc or the × to cancel the reply.
Sent replies show the quoted snippet above the bubble — click it (tooltip Scroll to original message) to jump to and briefly flash the original.
ch13-react.outcome: Reactions and replies broadcast to everyone in the room in real time.
ch13-react.note: The bot's messages can't be reacted to, and the whole hover bar is hidden while you're reviewing a finished meeting.

ch13-translate.heading: Auto-translate
ch13-translate.lead: Canvas M speaks three languages — Tiếng Việt, English and 한국어 — and the chat can translate every message into yours automatically.
ch13-translate.body: Your preferred language follows the app's own language picker, so there's no separate language selector in chat. The globe button in the header toggles translation on and off; its tooltip reads Auto-translate (on) or Auto-translate (off), and the button tints when active. With translation on, any message not already in your language shows the translated text on a second line beneath the original; while it's being fetched you briefly see Translating…. Senders pre-translate their messages on send, so in the common case the translation appears instantly with no extra wait. The toggle is remembered between sessions.

note.html: Turn it off if you'd rather read everyone's original wording, or to avoid the small translation latency. Messages already in your language never show a second line.

ch13-ref.heading: Composer controls and shortcuts
rows: Opens a quick-emoji palette; clicking an emoji inserts it into your draft at the cursor.
Inserts an @ and opens the mention picker for files and the bot.
Opens the image picker; selected images upload to the room library and are inserted as mention chips.
Sends the current draft (disabled when the draft is blank).
Insert a line break instead of sending.
Move the highlight in the open mention picker.
Insert the highlighted mention picker entry.
Close the mention picker, or cancel a pending reply.
Turn auto-translate on or off (remembered between sessions).
ch13-ref.note: Only images are accepted as attachments. The action row spaces the emoji, mention and attach buttons on the left and the Send button on the right.

host.html: There is no participant control to clear, delete or moderate chat history. The transcript and library content the bot draws on are governed by the meeting's lifecycle, not by individual participants.

ch13-trouble.heading: Chat troubleshooting

rows.sym: No composer, just an encryption message
rows.cause: You haven't started a live collaboration session yet
rows.fix: Start or join a live session; the composer appears once you're in the room

rows.sym: Composer replaced by a read-only notice
rows.cause: You opened a finished meeting for review
rows.fix: Finished meetings are immutable — history is extract-only, no new messages, reactions or replies

rows.sym: Attach skipped my file
rows.cause: Only image files are supported
rows.fix: An alert reads "Only images are supported. Skipped: …". Re-attach an image (PNG/JPG/etc.)

rows.sym: Mention chip does nothing / shows an alert
rows.cause: The referenced image isn't placed on the canvas yet
rows.fix: "This file isn't on the canvas yet. Open the library and click it to place first."

rows.sym: @bot apologised instead of answering
rows.cause: The AI had no useful answer, or the service/connection failed
rows.fix: Try again later; check your connection. Make sure your question is clear and follows @bot

rows.sym: Messages still in another language
rows.cause: Auto-translate is off, or the message is already in your language
rows.fix: Click the globe toggle until its tooltip reads "Auto-translate (on)"

ch13-trouble.note: If a translation seems stuck on "Translating…", it's fetching in the background — it resolves once the result returns or falls back to the original.

ch14-panel-open.heading: Show the Live transcript panel
steps: Find the floating Live transcript pill near the bottom-left of the canvas. A small number badge on it counts the segments captured so far.
Click it. The panel opens already scrolled to the newest line.
To start capturing your own voice, click STT: off so it becomes STT: on — your mic is now transcribed live.
To read everyone in your own language, click Translate: off so it becomes Translate: on; each finalised line gains an italic translation beneath it.
Drag the panel by its header to reposition it; drag the bottom-right corner to resize. Double-click the header to snap it back to the default size and place.
Click × (titled Hide (still logging in background)) to tuck the panel away. Recognition keeps running while it is hidden.
ch14-panel-open.outcome: The panel lists finalised lines with a speaker name, a clock time and — when translation is on and the language differs — a translated line beneath. Your own in-progress speech appears at the bottom marked speaking….
ch14-panel-open.note: Toggling STT or Translate here is the same switch the caption strip obeys. Turn translation on once and both surfaces speak your language.

host.html: Whether STT starts on for everyone by default is part of the host's meeting setup; as a participant you can always flip your own STT and Translate from this panel.

ch14-panel-open.figcap: The Live transcript panel, opened from the floating pill, with finalised lines and a live interim row.

ch14-controls.heading: Transcript panel reference
rows: Opens the panel. The badge shows how many segments exist.
Turns speech recognition of your mic on or off. Tooltip: Turn on/off speech recognition. Hidden in review (read-only) mode.
Translates each finalised segment into your preferred language. Tooltip: Translate transcript to preferred language.
Picks the recognition model; each option shows its per-minute price. Changing it restarts the live session. Hidden in review mode.
The language Deepgram transcribes your mic in — independent of the app's interface language. Changing it restarts your session.
Full shows the whole scrollable history; Compact shows only the 3 newest lines with trimmed chrome and hides the configuration row.
A testing aid: plays an audio file through the recognition pipeline. Hidden in review mode.
Closes the panel without stopping recognition.
Drag to resize; the panel remembers its size and position on this device.
ch14-controls.note: Your spoken-language, model, density and translate choices are saved per device, so they survive a reload. In Compact mode the whole settings row is hidden — switch back to Full to reach the model, language and test controls.

ch14-status.heading: What the status badge is telling you

tiles.cap: STT is on and your mic audio is genuinely flowing into recognition — a pulsing dot and three rippling level bars. This is the only state that proves the mic is actually being heard.

STT is on but nothing has reached it for a couple of seconds — a hollow amber ring. Usually a muted mic or a sound system that needs a tap to wake (common on iPad). Captions cannot appear until audio flows.
STT is off. Click STT: off to turn it on. The transcript body reads Turn on STT to start speech recognition.

ch14-status.useWhen: Glance at the pill in the panel header whenever captions or transcript lines are not appearing — it separates "off" from "on but silent" from "genuinely live." Two more pills appear during the testing flow: TEST (an audio file is playing through the pipeline) and ERROR (the test failed). When STT is on and waiting, the body shows Waiting for someone to speak….

ch14-dock.heading: Live captions over a shared screen
ch14-dock.lead: When someone shares a screen, a thin glass caption strip appears along the bottom of the shared view and shows the newest lines of whoever is speaking. It is on by default, so captions light up automatically — no hunting for a toggle.
ch14-dock.body: Each line carries the speaker's name in their personal colour, with a pulsing dot while they are still talking. After about four seconds of silence the strip collapses to a small CC puck and reappears on the next utterance. The strip rides whichever surface owns the view: the in-app viewer pane, the gallery, the presenter's picture-in-picture, or a plain overlay on the canvas. When you pop a shared screen out into its own window, the captions follow it there.

diagram.label: Caption strip controls
diagram.cap: On the strip: the CC button toggles captions; the 1 / 2 / 3 group sets how many lines show; the A / A / A group sets Small / Medium / Large text; the × hides the current strip until the next line. When CC is off, only a small CC puck remains so you can turn it back on.

note.html: The × on the strip is titled Hide captions for now — it dismisses the current strip but leaves captions on, so they return on the next sentence. The CC button actually turns the feature off. Captions follow the same translation toggle as the transcript panel: with Translate on you read everyone in your language; with it off you see their original words verbatim, never a blank line.

ch14-recording.heading: Who can record, and what you see
steps: Look in the bottom call-controls bar for a small red record-dot. If you are a participant (not the host) it is greyed out.
Hover it: the tooltip reads Only the host (Name) can record — this tells you who holds the control.
When the host starts recording, an inline pill appears in everyone's call bar: a pulsing red dot and a ticking timer such as 0:05.
Hover the pill as a participant to see Name is recording the meeting · 0:05. Your pill is read-only — it has no stop button.
When the host stops, the pill disappears for everyone. The recording file downloads to the host's device only.
ch14-recording.outcome: Recording state lives entirely in the call bar — there is no banner across the canvas. The same pill is shown to host and participants, so you always know when the meeting is being captured.

host.html: Only the host can start and stop recording, and the file saves to the host's machine. Recording captures audio (your mic plus peers) — it is separate from the text transcript, which any participant can keep with STT on.

ch14-trouble.heading: Captions & transcript troubleshooting

rows.sym: No lines appear, status reads No audio
rows.cause: Mic muted, or the audio context is suspended (common on iPad after switching tabs).
rows.fix: Unmute your mic and speak; tap the page if needed to wake audio. The pill turns to Live with rippling bars once audio flows.

rows.sym: Transcript body says Turn on STT to start speech recognition.
rows.cause: STT is off (status pill reads PAUSED).
rows.fix: Click STT: off in the panel so it reads STT: on.

rows.sym: Lines stay in another language
rows.cause: Translation is off, or the line is still an interim guess.
rows.fix: Click Translate: off so it reads Translate: on; interim (dimmed, italic) lines are never translated — wait for the final line.

rows.sym: Captions never appear over a shared screen
rows.cause: The CC button was switched off, leaving only the small CC puck.
rows.fix: Click the CC puck on the shared view to turn captions back on.

rows.sym: Captions vanish mid-conversation
rows.cause: Normal behaviour — the strip auto-hides after ~4 seconds of silence.
rows.fix: Nothing to do; the strip returns on the next utterance. Use the line-count and text-size controls if it feels too small.

rows.sym: I can't find a record button
rows.cause: Only the host can record; a participant's record-dot is disabled.
rows.fix: Ask the host to start recording. Hover the greyed dot to confirm who the host is.

rows.sym: STT WebSocket error / STT error in the panel footer
rows.cause: The recognition connection dropped or failed to configure.
rows.fix: Toggle STT off and on to restart the session; check your network. The footer surfaces these errors so a silent failure stays visible.

ch14-trouble.note: The No audio heartbeat exists precisely because "STT is on" never proved your mic was reaching recognition. When in doubt, trust the pulsing Live meter, not the toggle.

legend.text: Brand & top bar — the Canvas M wordmark on the left; the action cluster on the right (notifications, history, wallpaper, theme, language, Use the canvas solo, and your account chip).
Left sidebar — your views: My meetings and Invited / Upcoming, plus the list of Projects you belong to.
Middle column — the meeting cards for whatever you picked on the left. A header shows the context name, a Grid/List toggle, a Sort by menu and status filter chips.
Right calendar — a month calendar that always stays visible, tinted to match your meeting colours. Drag its left edge to make it wider or narrower.
Resume banner — appears above everything when you left a live meeting open and came back; one click drops you straight back in.

ch15-topbar.heading: Notifications, history, and your account
ch15-topbar.lead: The top bar carries the controls that belong to you, not to any single meeting. From left to right it reads as four clusters: a row of round icon buttons, the language capsule, the Use the canvas solo button, and finally your account chip.
ch15-topbar.body: The icon buttons are, in order: the bell (pending invitations, covered below), the history clock (My activity), the image tile (wallpaper), and the moon (light / dark theme). The history panel is a reverse-chronological log of what you did — it lists Created meeting, Invited to, Joined meeting and Uploaded to My Files rows, with an Accepted or Declined chip next to invitations you answered. When you have done nothing yet it simply reads No activity yet.
ch15-topbar.pull: The clock is your past; the bell is your to-do list. They are deliberately kept apart.

note.html: The wallpaper picker dresses the desk behind the glass panels. Pick any preset tile, or choose Tải ảnh lên (Upload image) to use your own photo — it applies instantly and is remembered on this browser. The small x on your uploaded tile returns you to the default. Wallpaper is purely cosmetic and only you see it.

ch15-sidebar.heading: Switching what the middle column shows
steps: Open My meetings to see your whole personal calendar of meetings — everything you organize or attend, across every project.
Open Invited / Upcoming to see only the meetings you were invited to. This view never shows an edit pencil — you do not edit a meeting you were merely invited to.
Scroll to the Projects heading to see the projects you belong to. Each row may show a colour dot and the project's stage; a project you were only invited into carries an Invited badge instead.
Click any project to list just its meetings. The project name becomes the column title.
ch15-sidebar.outcome: The middle column reloads for whatever you picked, and any open detail or form is cleared so you never see a stale view.
ch15-sidebar.note: If the project list can't load, the empty slot says Couldn't load — check your network connection. with a Retry link, rather than pretending you have no projects.

host.html: Internal staff also see My Files, Guest manager and Manage projects entries here, plus a New project button at the bottom. As a participant these are hidden — projects are created and run for you.

ch15-cards.heading: Reading and opening a card
steps: Each card shows the meeting's title (optional emoji icon and topic), its date and time, the creator (avatar + name), a coloured status pill, and — in the overview and invited lists — a clickable project chip.
Click the body of a card to open the meeting. A live or scheduled one joins you; a finished one opens read-only for review.
Click the project chip on a card to jump straight to that project's list instead of opening the meeting.
Use Grid / List in the header to switch the layout, and Sort by to order by By time, By title or By status.
Use the status chips — All, Live, Upcoming, Done, Cancelled — to narrow the list to one lifecycle stage.
ch15-cards.outcome: When sorted By time the list groups by day with Today / Tomorrow / date separators — upcoming days first (nearest first), then past days (most recent first).
ch15-cards.figcap: The Invited / Upcoming view, with each card's status pill and creator.
ch15-cards.note: Two small icon buttons on every card — a Palette and a Details (eye) — let you tint the card or open its full detail panel. If the cards can't load you'll see Couldn't load — check your network connection. with Retry; an empty list reads No meetings in this project yet.

ch15-cardstates.heading: The colours a card can wear

tiles.cap: A green Live pill and a pulsing live dot. Clicking the card joins the meeting in progress.
An Upcoming card carries a Scheduled pill and its planned date and time. Joining goes through the start gate until the host begins.
A Finished or Cancelled pill marks a closed meeting. Opening it shows the canvas read-only — you can review and extract, but not change anything.

ch15-cardstates.useWhen: Glance at the pill before you click: green means walk straight in, a date means it has not started, and a grey pill means review-only.

ch15-bell.heading: Invitations that need your answer
ch15-bell.lead: The bell collects every meeting invitation still waiting on your reply, so none slip past. A small numbered badge shows how many are pending; click it to open the Notifications & invitations panel.
ch15-bell.body: Each row shows the meeting title, when it is (or a red LIVE NOW tag if it is already running), and the project name. Two buttons sit on the right: Accept and Decline. Accepting a meeting that is live counts as "I'm coming" and joins you on the spot; accepting a scheduled one simply confirms your seat. Declining removes the row and quietly confirms with Invitation declined. When nothing is pending the panel reads No notifications.

note.html: An invitation grants access but sends no email or push — the bell is the notification channel, refreshed automatically about once a minute. The bell only ever lists things you can still act on; finished and cancelled meetings drop off by themselves.

ch15-resume.eyebrow: Picking up where you left off
ch15-resume.heading: The Resume banner
ch15-resume.lead: If you closed the tab or refreshed while a meeting was still going, the dashboard greets you with a Resume meeting banner above the columns, showing the meeting's title. One click takes you straight back in.
ch15-resume.body: The banner is careful: it only appears for a meeting that is genuinely resumable. A meeting that has since been ended for everyone, or cancelled, never offers Resume — the banner re-checks the meeting's real status when you return to the tab, and quietly removes itself if the meeting is over. A scheduled meeting that has not started yet is not offered either; you join those through the normal start gate.

note.html: Separately, the Use the canvas solo button in the top bar drops you onto a blank private canvas with no meeting and nobody else — handy for a quick sketch. Leaving it returns you to the dashboard.

ch15-statuses.heading: Meeting lifecycle and what you can do
rows: Goes through the start gate; you wait until the host starts
Pulsing live dot; LIVE NOW in the bell
Opens read-only — review and extract only
Opens read-only; the organizer cancelled it
ch15-statuses.note: These four are the only canonical statuses. Older meetings may carry legacy labels, but Canvas M maps them onto this set so the pill is always one of these four.

host.html: Starting a scheduled meeting, ending one for everyone, cancelling and restoring are organizer / project-authority actions. As a participant you only ever join, review, or answer an invitation.

ch15-trouble.heading: Dashboard troubleshooting

rows.sym: The middle column shows "Couldn't load"
rows.cause: The server didn't respond when fetching your meetings or projects
rows.fix: Click Retry; check your internet connection if it keeps failing

rows.sym: A card won't open
rows.cause: The room couldn't be reached or you don't have access
rows.fix: You'll see "Couldn't open the meeting…"; confirm you were invited and try again

rows.sym: An invitation isn't in the bell
rows.cause: It's already finished, cancelled, or you already answered or joined
rows.fix: The bell only lists open, unanswered invitations; check the card in your lists instead

rows.sym: The Resume banner disappeared
rows.cause: The host ended or cancelled the meeting while you were away
rows.fix: Expected — the banner re-checks status on focus and drops dead meetings

rows.sym: No "New meeting" or project tools
rows.cause: Those are organizer / internal-staff controls
rows.fix: Ask a host to schedule the meeting and invite you

ch15-trouble.note: Most dashboard errors are transient network hiccups — a Retry usually clears them. If sign-in itself fails, that's covered earlier in the login chapter.

ch16-overview.heading: Six tabs, one window
ch16-overview.lead: Account settings is the single place to manage yourself. It opens as a Glass-Desk panel titled Account settings, with a tab rail down the left and the chosen tab's controls on the right. A close button labelled Close sits top-right, and pressing Esc — or clicking the dimmed area outside the card — dismisses the whole window.
ch16-overview.body: The rail shows up to six tabs: Profile, Account, Security, Preferences, My data, and Privacy. Which tab you land on depends on how you opened the window — clicking your own avatar in the participants bar, or the "set up your profile" nudge, jumps straight to Profile; the gear and the account menu open it the same way. Each time the window opens it re-seeds from your stored profile, so a half-finished edit you abandoned never carries over.

note.html: If you joined by magic link rather than a password, the Security tab is hidden — there is no password to change. Magic-link logins are also a no-op for the parts of My data they cannot read; a list you have no access to simply shows its empty state rather than an error.

legend.text: Window title — Account settings.
Close button (top-right X). Esc or an outside click does the same.
Tab rail: Profile, Account, Security, Preferences, My data, Privacy.
The active tab's panel — controls render on the right.
Profile preview: avatar, display name, and company, updating live as you type.

ch16-avatars.heading: Three ways to set your avatar

tiles.cap: Eight built-in tiles. Click one to select it (a selected ring appears); it is stored as a lib: reference and syncs to your account across devices.
⬆ Upload image opens a file picker (images only). The picture is auto-resized to 256 px on its longest edge and kept on this device. A Remove button appears once an avatar is set.
With no avatar chosen — or after pressing Remove — your tile falls back to a generated avatar built from your name and email.

ch16-avatars.useWhen: Use a gallery tile if you want the same face on every device you sign in from; upload an image when you want your real photo, accepting that it stays local to this browser.

ch16-account.heading: Your organisation details (read-only)
rows: Your job title from the org directory.
