Your access role — falls back to Staff if none is set.
ch16-account.note: These fields are system-managed and cannot be edited here: The organisation details below are system-managed — read-only here. They load from the org record; if that lookup fails you see Couldn't load account info. Showing your sign-in session. and the panel falls back to your verified sign-in session so it still shows something. Any field with no value displays as a dash (—).

host.html: These details are owned by the organisation system, not by hosts or admins inside the app. To correct a wrong title or division, contact whoever administers your org directory.

ch16-security.heading: Change your password, or sign out
steps: Open the Security tab (password logins only — guests don't see it).
Type your existing password into Current password.
Type the new one into New password, then again into Confirm new password.
Press Save password. The button reads Saving… while it works.
On success a green banner reads Password changed. and the three fields clear.
ch16-security.outcome: Your current password is verified first by re-authenticating, then the new one is set — so even on an already-signed-in browser nobody can change your password without knowing the old one.
ch16-security.note: New passwords must be at least 8 characters (New password must be at least 8 characters.) and the two new fields must match (Confirmation doesn't match.). A wrong current password gives Current password is incorrect.; a password that fails policy (or equals the old one) shows the server's reason or Couldn't change password. Try again. Save password stays disabled until all three fields have text. The Sign out button at the bottom ends your session immediately.
ch16-security.figcap: Change password: current, new, confirm — then Save password.

ch16-preferences.heading: Every per-device preference, grouped
rows: Applies to the whole app interface, including Excalidraw's own menus.
App colour scheme; System follows your OS.
Auto-translate incoming chat into your language.
When on, your mic is transcribed live.
The language your mic is transcribed in.
Translate each finalised transcript segment into your language.
How the live transcript panel is laid out.
Auto-show the caption strip when someone shares a screen.
How many lines the caption strip keeps on screen.
Virtual background for your outgoing camera. Desktop only.
Your own ceiling for the outgoing camera; quality still floats below it on a weak network.
ch16-preferences.note: Interface preferences (language, theme, captions) are kept on this device only. Every control here is the same one used inline elsewhere, so a change takes effect immediately — including mid-call, if your camera is already on. Background effects are desktop-only: on iPad or phone web the picker renders greyed out with the note Background effects are only supported on desktop. If an admin has lowered the max video quality, tiers above the cap are greyed and a note reads Admin caps the max at {level} — Auto always stays selectable and simply rides the cap.

host.html: The video-quality cap shown here is set org-wide by an admin; you can pick any tier up to it but not above. There is no participant control to raise the cap.

ch16-privacy.heading: Microphone consent and what we keep
ch16-privacy.lead: The Privacy tab gives you a single, plain-language consent switch and a note describing the data the app holds. The toggle is labelled Allow mic transcription (Deepgram): when on, your mic audio is sent to Deepgram for live transcription; when off, nothing is sent.
ch16-privacy.body: This is the same on/off state as Enable mic for STT in Preferences — flipping it here also flips it there, and vice versa. Turning it off is an immediate, complete opt-out: no audio leaves your device for transcription.

note.html: The note reads: We store your profile (name, company, avatar), a log of meetings you join, files you upload, and transcripts while you have STT on. Interface preferences (language, theme, captions) are kept on this device only. Your My data tab lets you review the lists behind this — your meetings, invitations, and files — each read-only, with empty states (No meetings yet., No invitations yet., No files yet.) when there is nothing to show and Loading… while they fetch.

ch16-trouble.heading: Settings troubleshooting

rows.sym: Save on the Profile tab is greyed out
rows.cause: Display name is blank (or only spaces).
rows.fix: Type a non-blank display name; Save enables once it has real text.

rows.sym: No Security tab in the rail
rows.cause: You signed in by magic link, which has no password.
rows.fix: Expected for guests. Password changes only apply to password logins.

rows.sym: Account fields all show a dash and a yellow banner
rows.cause: The org record lookup failed; the panel fell back to your session.
rows.fix: Reopen later; the banner reads Couldn't load account info… and your verified session values still appear.

rows.sym: Background picker is greyed out
rows.cause: You're on iPad or phone web, where background effects aren't supported.
rows.fix: Use a desktop browser; the note Background effects are only supported on desktop explains the limit.

rows.sym: High video-quality tiers are dim and unclickable
rows.cause: An admin lowered the org-wide max video-quality cap.
rows.fix: Pick a tier at or below the cap, or Auto. The note names the cap.

rows.sym: Uploaded avatar isn't on my other device
rows.cause: Uploaded images are kept on this device only; only gallery picks sync.
rows.fix: Choose a built-in gallery tile to have an avatar follow your login.

rows.sym: Only image files are accepted. after uploading
rows.cause: The chosen file wasn't an image.
rows.fix: Pick a picture file (PNG, JPG, etc.).

ch16-trouble.note: Closing the window discards nothing already saved — preference toggles and password changes commit the moment you make them; only an unsaved Profile edit is dropped, and reopening re-seeds the stored values.

ch17-three-exits.heading: Three ways to step out — and they are not the same
ch17-three-exits.lead: Canvas M deliberately gives leaving three distinct verbs, each with its own glyph in the header, so you never confuse a small step back with shutting the whole room down.
ch17-three-exits.body: Leave call (a hang-up handset in the media group) only drops you out of the live audio/video — you stay in the meeting, the canvas is still live, and you can rejoin the call with Join. Leave (an arrow-out-of-box icon, far right) exits the meeting room entirely: your canvas is saved, the room is cleared from the URL so you won't auto-rejoin on reload, and you land back on your project home. Everyone else stays. End meeting (a red power icon) is the host-only kill switch — it finishes the meeting for everyone at once.
ch17-three-exits.pull: Leave call = hang up. Leave = walk out. End meeting = power off the room.

diagram.label: The three exit glyphs
diagram.cap: Left to right: hang-up (Leave call), arrow-out (Leave), red power (End meeting).

note.html: The red End meeting button only appears for the host, organiser, co-host, or a project authority. If you don't see it, you can't end the meeting for everyone — and that's by design. The server enforces the same rule, so the button's absence is not the only guard.

ch17-ended.heading: When the host ends the meeting
ch17-ended.lead: Ending is the host's call, and it's final. When the host clicks End meeting, they first confirm the prompt “End the meeting for EVERYONE? All participants switch to read-only review.” — and that's exactly what happens to you.
ch17-ended.body: Within a second or two, your meeting flips into review mode without dropping you. The canvas becomes read-only, a banner appears across the top, and the meeting is marked finished. You don't get kicked out — you can stay and read the record, download the transcript, or step out with Leave whenever you're ready. Behind the scenes the meeting is recorded as finished so that re-opening it later always lands you back in this same read-only review.

note.html: Ending also kicks off an automatic AI recap from the transcript and chat — it runs in the background and never delays the meeting from ending. You'll find that recap surfaced later in the meeting's detail view.

ch17-review-states.heading: What review mode locks — and what it leaves open

tiles.cap: A status banner reads “Reviewing (read-only) · meeting finished — extract only” with an eye icon, pinned to the canvas so you always know the meeting is frozen.
The conversation panel shows “Reviewing a finished meeting — chat is read-only”. You can read every message but can't send new ones.
Uploads are disabled: “The meeting has finished — the library is read-only, uploads are disabled.” Existing files stay viewable.

ch17-review-states.useWhen: You'll see all three together the moment a meeting finishes — whether the host ended it live, or you opened a finished meeting from your portal or project list. Content-creating tools (stickers, the canvas bot, text translation) are hidden, and you can't present or edit the meeting's title.

ch17-log.heading: Reading the transcript & generating a summary
steps: Open the log from the header's Transcript button (the document icon — it shows a count badge when there's a transcript).
The log opens on the Transcript tab: the full conversation, grouped by speaker with avatars, timestamps, and a per-line language tag.
Switch to the Summary tab. If none exists yet, click Generate summary — Gemini reads the full transcript and returns an overview, participants, key topics, decisions, and action items.
Watch for “Generating summary… (~5-15s for long meetings)”; a dot appears on the Summary tab once it's ready.
Click Download .md to save the current tab (transcript or summary) as a Markdown file.
Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> or click outside the modal to close it.
ch17-log.outcome: You've read the record and, if you wanted, pulled a structured recap and a downloadable copy — without changing anything in the finished meeting.

host.html: In a live meeting the footer also offers Clear log (wipes the transcript and summary for the room after a confirm) and Regenerate summary. Both are hidden in review — a finished meeting is extract-only, so you can read and download but never rewrite the record.

ch17-log.figcap: The meeting log modal: Transcript and Summary tabs, with download in the footer.

ch17-log-ref.heading: Every button in the meeting log
rows: Full chronological transcript, grouped by speaker
AI overview, topics, decisions, action items
Asks Gemini for a recap of the transcript
Replaces an existing summary with a fresh one
Saves the active tab as a Markdown file
Wipes transcript + summary for the room (confirm)
ch17-log-ref.note: The transcript only fills up while someone has speech-to-text turned on during the call. An empty log reads “No transcript yet. Join a call + turn on STT to start recording.”

host.html: Clearing a log empties what you see immediately, but the stored transcript blob still exists — rejoining the room re-hydrates it.

ch17-trouble.heading: Leaving & review troubleshooting

rows.sym: No red End meeting button
rows.cause: You're not the host, organiser, co-host, or project authority
rows.fix: Only those roles can end a meeting for everyone. Use Leave to exit yourself; ask the host to end it.

rows.sym: Meeting suddenly went read-only
rows.cause: The host ended the meeting
rows.fix: Expected. You're now in review — read the transcript, download it, or click Leave. Nothing you do can edit it.

rows.sym: Can't type in chat
rows.cause: The meeting is finished (review mode)
rows.fix: Chat is read-only in a finished meeting by design. You can still read every message.

rows.sym: Can't upload a file
rows.cause: Review mode disables the library
rows.fix: Uploads are off in a finished meeting — the library is read-only. Open existing files to view them.

rows.sym: Summary tab is empty
rows.cause: No summary generated yet
rows.fix: Click Generate summary on the Summary tab. Hidden in review — read or download instead.

rows.sym: “Couldn't end the meeting — check your network and try again.”
rows.cause: The finish write to the server failed (host action)
rows.fix: Nothing changed; the host can simply retry End meeting.

rows.sym: Re-opened a meeting and it's read-only
rows.cause: The meeting is finished — it always opens for review
rows.fix: Expected. A finished meeting is immutable and extract-only every time you open it.

ch17-trouble.note: Leaving never loses work — your canvas is saved before the room closes. Ending is the only irreversible exit, and only a host can do it.

ch18-mindset.heading: The app tells you what's wrong
ch18-mindset.lead: Canvas M rarely fails silently. When a control can't do its job, it changes shape, turns colour, or carries a short message you can read by resting your pointer on it. Before you reach for a reload, read what the button is already telling you.
ch18-mindset.body: Three places carry the truth. Tooltips appear when you hover an icon in the meeting header — the mic, camera, and call buttons all describe their current state and what a click will do. Toasts slide in briefly for one-off failures, such as a screen-share that wouldn't start. Full-screen cards take over when you can't enter a room at all — the start gate and the waiting room each explain why and offer the next step. Match the wording you see to the tables in this chapter; the exact text is the key.
ch18-mindset.pull: Read the button before you reload it.

diagram.label: Where messages surface
diagram.cap: Header tooltips for live controls, toasts for transient errors, and full-screen gate cards for entry blocks.

note.html: Many controls that look broken are simply Host-only. If a button is greyed with a tooltip naming someone else — for example “{host} is recording the meeting” or “{name} is presenting — wait for them to finish” — nothing is wrong; that action belongs to the host or the current presenter.

ch18-micstates.heading: Every call-button state, at a glance

tiles.cap: Open-door icon. You're in the room but not in the audio/video call yet. Click to join listening-only.
Accent mic = you can speak; click to Mute. Red MicOff = muted or listen-only.
No mic on this device. The mic button is disabled and labelled listen-only; you still hear everyone.
Single red MicOff button. The tooltip names the cause; clicking it retries the join.
A disabled spinner button while the call hooks up or the mic prompt is open.
VideoOff by default; click to turn the camera on. A spinner shows while it starts.

ch18-micstates.useWhen: Use this to identify which state your call button is in before matching a row in the tables — the icon and colour tell you as much as the tooltip.

ch18-camera.heading: Camera won't turn on

rows.sym: Camera button is greyed and tooltip reads “No camera detected on this device”
rows.cause: Canvas M probed for a camera when the call went live and found none, so the toggle is disabled.
rows.fix: Connect a webcam, then leave and rejoin the call so the device is re-probed. The audio call keeps working without a camera.

rows.sym: Tooltip reads “Couldn't start the camera — check permissions and retry.”
rows.cause: The camera exists but failed to start — usually a denied permission or another app holding it.
rows.fix: Allow the camera in your browser's site settings (or close the other app), then click the camera button again.

rows.sym: Camera button shows a spinner and won't respond
rows.cause: The camera is in its starting state. The toggle is disabled until it resolves to on or off.
rows.fix: Wait a moment. If it never settles, leave and rejoin the call.

rows.sym: Background blur or image options are missing or greyed
rows.cause: Background effects are desktop-only. The tooltip reads “Background effects are only supported on desktop”.
rows.fix: Use a laptop or desktop to change or blur your camera background. Your saved choice auto-applies when the camera turns on.

ch18-camera.note: Turning the camera on never disturbs your audio: it opts in on the same call, defaulting to off. If permission is denied the tile simply keeps showing your avatar.

rows.sym: Lobby shows “That link or room code isn't valid.”
rows.cause: The link or code you pasted into Paste a link or room code to join didn't parse as a meeting.
rows.fix: Re-copy the full invite link and paste it again. Ask the host to resend if it still fails.

rows.sym: Full-screen card: “Meeting hasn't started yet” with a spinner and “Waiting for the host to start the meeting…”
rows.cause: You opened a scheduled meeting before the host pressed start. Canvas M polls and joins you automatically the moment it goes live.
rows.fix: Leave the card open and wait — you'll be pulled in as soon as it starts. Use Back to home if you'd rather wait elsewhere.

rows.sym: Card: “Waiting to be let in” with “Waiting for the host to let you in…”
rows.cause: As an external guest, you knocked on a live meeting with a waiting room. Internal staff skip this; guests wait to be admitted.
rows.fix: Wait — Canvas M polls your knock and admits you automatically once the host accepts. It shows who you're “Joining as” while you wait.

rows.sym: Card: “Not admitted” with “The host hasn't let you in right now. You can knock again in a moment.”
rows.cause: The host denied your knock, or you're inside the 30-second re-knock cooldown.
rows.fix: Click Knock again. If it doesn't take, wait a few seconds for the cooldown and retry; the button reads “Knocking…” while it sends.

rows.sym: Card: “Meeting cancelled” — “The organizer cancelled this meeting.”
rows.cause: The organizer cancelled this meeting; there is nothing live to join.
rows.fix: Click Back to home. Watch your invitations for a rescheduled time.

rows.sym: Card: “Meeting has ended” — “This meeting has ended. The organizer will share a recap with you separately.”
rows.cause: The meeting finished. Internal members open it read-only for review; guests see only this notice.
rows.fix: Nothing to do — wait for the host's recap. Internal members can reopen it from the project for read-only review.

rows.sym: Banner: “The host removed you from the meeting.”
rows.cause: The host removed you from the room.
rows.fix: Nothing in-app overrides this. If it was a mistake, ask the host to re-invite you.

rows.sym: Error toast: “Couldn't verify the meeting state (lost connection to the server). Try again later.”
rows.cause: Canvas M lost its connection to the server while checking whether the meeting could be joined.
rows.fix: Check your network and try again later. A reload re-runs the check from a clean state.

note.html: The Start meeting button and the admit / deny waiting-room controls are Host-only — they only appear for the owning department (organizer, host, co-host, or a same-department member). If you don't see Start meeting, you're not expected to; simply wait.

ch18-share.heading: Screen sharing won't start

rows.sym: Present button is greyed with tooltip “Screen sharing isn't supported on this device or browser (e.g. iPad / iPhone). Present from a computer instead.”
rows.cause: Your browser doesn't offer the screen-capture API. iPad and iPhone Safari can't share a screen at all.
rows.fix: Present from a computer instead. Open the same meeting link on a laptop or desktop to share.

rows.sym: Present button is disabled while someone else is sharing
rows.cause: Only one person presents at a time. The presenter's tooltip reads “{name} is presenting — wait for them to finish”.
rows.fix: Wait for the current presenter to stop. The button frees up the moment they end their share.

rows.sym: Toast: “Couldn't present your screen.” (with extra detail)
rows.cause: The browser's screen-picker was cancelled or the capture failed to start.
rows.fix: Click Present again and pick a window or screen in the browser dialog. Don't dismiss the picker.

rows.sym: Toast: “Couldn't share your screen”
rows.cause: The screen track errored after it started.
rows.fix: Stop and restart the share. If it keeps failing, reload and rejoin the call before presenting.

rows.sym: Shared screen shows “Connecting…” and doesn't appear
rows.cause: The presenter's screen track is still being negotiated.
rows.fix: Wait a moment — it resolves on its own. If it never paints, ask the presenter to stop and re-share.

ch18-share.note: When you do present, you'll see You are presenting; others see {name} is presenting. Use Pop out to drag the shared view to a second screen, or Stop sharing to end it.

ch18-files.heading: A file won't open or upload

rows.sym: Toast: “Only images, DXF, PDF and IFC are supported for now. Skipped: {name}”
rows.cause: You dropped a file type the room library doesn't handle. Unsupported files are skipped.
rows.fix: Convert to an image, PDF, DXF, or IFC and upload again. The upload bar lists the accepted types.

rows.sym: Toast: “Couldn't process IFC file: {name}”
rows.cause: The IFC model couldn't be parsed — usually a corrupt or unsupported export.
rows.fix: Re-export the IFC from your BIM tool and upload again.

rows.sym: 3D pane shows “Couldn't read IFC model” or CAD pane shows “Couldn't read DXF”
rows.cause: The viewer failed to load the file's geometry. The detail follows the message.
rows.fix: Close the pane and reopen the file. If it still fails, re-export and re-upload it.

rows.sym: Pane reads “Maximum 3D models already open. Close another file to view this one.” (or the DXF equivalent)
rows.cause: You've hit the limit of simultaneously open 3D/CAD viewers.
rows.fix: Close an open IFC or DXF tab, then open the new one.

rows.sym: Viewer sits on “Waiting for IFC file from peer…” (also for DXF / PDF)
rows.cause: Another participant opened the file; your copy is still streaming over from them.
rows.fix: Wait — it loads once the transfer completes. If it stalls, ask them to re-open it.

rows.sym: Deleting a library file warns “This file is locked by {lockedBy}. Ask them to unlock it first.”
rows.cause: Someone locked the file to stop accidental deletion.
rows.fix: Ask the person who locked it (or the original uploader) to unlock it, then delete.

rows.sym: My Files: “Upload failed: {name}” or “File too large (max 50MB): {name}”
rows.cause: The upload to your personal shelf failed, or the file exceeds the 50MB limit.
rows.fix: Check your connection and retry; for oversized files, compress or split below 50MB.

rows.sym: Picker: “Couldn't load the file from your shelf: {name}”
rows.cause: Copying a shelf file into the meeting failed mid-transfer.
rows.fix: Try the file again from My Files. A reload of the meeting also clears a stuck copy.

note.html: If a meeting has finished and you reopen it for review, the library turns read-only: “The meeting has finished — the library is read-only, uploads are disabled.” That's expected, not a fault.

ch18-captions.heading: Captions or transcript aren't appearing

rows.sym: Transcript panel reads “Turn on STT to start speech recognition.” with a PAUSED badge
rows.cause: Speech-to-text is off. Captions and the live transcript both depend on it.
rows.fix: Toggle STT: on in the transcript panel. The badge changes from PAUSED to LIVE.

rows.sym: Badge reads No audio even though STT is on
rows.cause: STT is on but no audio is reaching it — usually a muted mic, or a suspended audio context on iPad.
rows.fix: Unmute your mic. On iPad, tap the page once to wake the audio context.

rows.sym: Transcript shows “Waiting for someone to speak…” and never fills
rows.cause: STT is live but no one is speaking, or no mic audio is being captured.
rows.fix: If you expect captions of your own voice, confirm your mic is unmuted and the badge reads Live.

rows.sym: Panel shows “STT error” or “STT WebSocket error” (badge ERROR)
rows.cause: The connection to the speech service dropped or failed to open.
rows.fix: Toggle STT off and on to reconnect. If it persists, reload and rejoin the call.

rows.sym: Panel reads “Failed to load STT worklet: {message}”
rows.cause: The audio-processing module the browser needs for STT failed to load.
rows.fix: Reload the page so the worklet re-downloads, then turn STT on again.

rows.sym: Meeting log is empty: “No transcript yet. Join a call + turn on STT to start recording.”
rows.cause: No segments were captured — either no one had STT on, or the call was never joined.
rows.fix: Join the audio call and turn on STT so future speech is recorded into the log.

rows.sym: Captions don't show even with STT on
rows.cause: The caption strip can be hidden, or set to auto-show only while presenting.
rows.fix: Turn on Captions (CC) in the header (it toggles between “Turn on captions (CC)” and “Turn off captions (CC)”). Check Show captions while presenting in Settings → Preferences.

ch18-captions.note: Speech-to-text needs your consent. In Settings → Privacy, Allow mic transcription (Deepgram) must be on; off means nothing from your mic is sent and you'll never see your own captions.

ch18-statusref.heading: Status badges and what they mean
rows: Speech-to-text is on and the session is connected.
Your mic audio is actively flowing into transcription right now.
STT is on but no audio is reaching it — muted mic or suspended context.
Speech-to-text is turned off; turn it on to capture speech.
The speech connection failed; toggle STT off and on to retry.
You're running an audio file through STT to check accuracy, not a live mic.
You're in the call with no usable mic — you hear everyone but can't speak.
You're viewing the canvas but haven't joined a live room yet.
The meeting finished; you can extract content but not edit, chat, or upload.
ch18-statusref.note: Badges are status, not errors — most need no action. Only ERROR and No audio ask you to do something.

host.html: Recording carries its own badges: a non-host sees “{host} is recording the meeting” and the record button stays disabled. Starting and stopping a recording is Host-only.

ch19-mental.heading: Two doors into one project
ch19-mental.lead: A project name appears in two places in the left sidebar, and they do different things. Knowing which is which saves a lot of hunting for controls that aren't where you expect.
ch19-mental.body: Clicking a project under the Projects heading in the sidebar takes you to that project's meeting list — a clean view of its cards, with a small ⚙ shortcut in the title row. That view holds no administration. All of it — create, edit metadata, members, guests, delete — lives on the separate Manage projects page, reached from the Manage projects sidebar item. The rule of thumb: the sidebar project link means “go to its meetings”; the Manage projects page means “administer it.” Creating a project just opens a personal folder where you become its leader and owner — it grants no power over anyone else's projects.

note.html: Manage projects, Guest manager and My Files appear in the sidebar only for internal staff accounts. A guest never sees them. The server enforces the same gate, so the page is genuinely staff-only, not merely hidden.

ch19-find.heading: Open the Manage projects page
steps: In the left sidebar, look below My meetings and Invited / Upcoming for the Manage projects item (folder-kanban icon).
Click it. The middle column switches to the project management page, titled Manage projects.
At the top sits a Search projects… box, a grid/list View toggle, and a New project button.
Projects are grouped: My projects (folders you belong to) and Invited (folders another department invited you into for one meeting), each with a count.
Click any project tile or row to drill into its detail. Click All projects to come back to the list.
ch19-find.outcome: You're on the dedicated admin surface. The grid (card) view is the default — covers carry the page; the list view is a denser alternative.
ch19-find.note: The toolbar (search + view toggle + New project) hides entirely when you have no projects yet — the empty state carries its own create button instead.
ch19-find.figcap: The Manage projects page: search, view toggle, and grouped project tiles.

ch19-fields.heading: Project metadata fields
rows: The only required field. Shown everywhere the project appears.
Upload an image; it becomes the tile cover and the detail hero, with the name laid over it.
Placeholder “Client / owner”. Searchable; shown in the detail's Details grid.
Placeholder “Studio / office”. Shown as Branch / office in the detail.
Dropdown: Concept · Schematic design · Design development · Construction docs · Construction · Handover. Shown as the stage pill.
Dropdown: Residential · Commercial · Mixed-use · Public · Industrial · Other.
Free text (multiline). Falls back to “No description” where meta is shown.
ch19-fields.note: The Phase and Type dropdowns keep any older free-text value selectable, so a legacy stage like a hand-typed phase isn't lost when you edit. The leading department is set automatically to the department of whoever created the project and is read-only — it isn't a field you fill in.

host.html: The Search projects… box matches against the name, code, client and location — so a project code or client name finds the folder fast.

legend.text: All projects — the back link (chevron-left) that returns you to the grouped list.
Hero — the cover image (or a letter initial), the project name with its icon, the stage pill and the code.
Cosmetic accents — a palette (“Đổi màu dự án” / change project colour) and a smiley (“Gán biểu tượng dự án” / assign project icon). Any member may set these; hidden for invitee-only folders.
Edit project and View meetings → — edit metadata (managers only) and jump to this project's meeting list.
Details section — Client, Location, Branch / office, Project type, Created, Leader, the description, and the read-only Leading department.
Members, Project guests and the collapsible Danger zone follow — each a native expand/collapse section.

ch19-edit.heading: Edit a project's metadata
steps: Open the project on the Manage projects page so its detail is showing.
In the hero, click Edit project (pencil). It appears only for managers, and never on an invitee-only folder.
The same field modal opens, now titled Edit project, pre-filled with the current values.
Adjust any field and click Save.
On success the modal closes and the detail refreshes.
ch19-edit.outcome: Your changes are saved in one call (unlike create, which is two steps). The stage pill, code and Details grid update to match.
ch19-edit.note: If the save fails, the modal stays open — your edits aren't silently lost — and an alert reads “Save failed — …”. Fix the cause (usually network or permission) and Save again.

host.html: If you were only invited into a project for one meeting, its detail shows the banner “You're invited to this project — view only” and no edit, members or guest controls appear.

ch19-members.heading: Build the member roster
steps: In the project detail, expand the Members section. Members are grouped by department, each as a full row: avatar, name, title chip and role badge.
Click Add member to open the staff picker, select one or more internal colleagues, and confirm. The roster reloads with them added.
To remove someone, click the ✕ on their row and confirm “Remove {name} from the project?”. The leader (owner) can't be removed — their row has no remove action.
Leadership can promote a participant with Make co-operator (shield), or demote one with Remove co-operator.
The leading-division head (or an admin) can hand over leadership with Assign project leader (crown), confirming “Make {name} the new project leader?”.
Use Add guest (next to Add member) to jump straight to the Project guests section's issue form.
ch19-members.outcome: The roster reflects exactly who may see the whole folder. Roles drive what each person can do; the next table spells them out.
ch19-members.note: Only internal colleagues can be added — the picker is drawn from the staff directory. If a member add is rejected, the alert reads “Couldn't add member (internal emails only).”

host.html: A plain participant sees the roster read-only: no Add, no Remove, no promote/demote. The promote and assign-leader buttons appear only for the relevant authority tier.

ch19-roles.heading: Project roles & who can do what
cols: Can manage (members, guests, edit, delete meetings)?
rows: Yes — full management of the project.
Yes — delete the project, promote/demote co-operators (delegation). Defaults to the creator.
Yes — add/remove members, edit metadata, organise meetings.
No — a co-operator can't delete the project or change other roles.
No — sees the roster read-only and may join meetings.
Yes, on every project of their department — the head is the supreme authority tier.
Yes — may assign/replace the project leader and delegate co-operators.
n/a — a title never grants or locks any project action.
ch19-roles.note: The role badge (Leader / Co-operator / Participant), the org-authority badge (Division admin) and the title chip are three separate things. A title or being a department head never locks the Make co-operator or Assign project leader buttons — authority and project role are independent axes. Only the current leader's row is fixed: the system refuses to re-role the owner.

host.html: Every one of these checks is enforced by the server, not just hidden in the UI. The buttons you see reflect what the server will actually allow for your account.

ch19-cosmetic.heading: Set a project colour & icon
steps: On a project tile (or in the detail hero), click the palette button — tooltip “Đổi màu dự án” (change project colour).
Pick a colour from the menu; choose Default to clear it. The tile and its sidebar dot tint immediately, with no list flash.
Click the smiley button — tooltip “Gán biểu tượng dự án” (assign project icon) — to pick an emoji from the project presets; choose the clear option to remove it.
The colour and icon appear on the project's tile, its sidebar entry, and on every meeting card inside it.
ch19-cosmetic.outcome: The folder gets a glanceable accent that flows through to its meeting cards. Any member may set these — they're cosmetic, exempt from the owner-only guard.
ch19-cosmetic.note: If a cosmetic save fails, the toast reads “Không lưu được màu/biểu tượng dự án” (couldn't save the project's colour/icon). The accent simply isn't applied; nothing else changes.

host.html: The palette and emoji buttons are hidden on an invitee-only folder — there's nothing there for a guest department to restyle.

ch19-states.heading: What the list shows

tiles.cap: Folders you belong to, sorted by most recently updated, under the My projects (n) heading. Tiles show cover, name, stage pill and a code · client · location meta line.
Folders another department invited you into for one meeting, under Invited (n), each badged Invited. These open read-only — no admin.
A folder-kanban illustration with “No projects yet” and the hint “Create your first project to start organizing meetings.”, plus a New project button.

ch19-states.useWhen: When a search matches nothing you'll instead see “No projects match "{q}"” with a Clear search link. If the list itself fails to load, it reads “Couldn't load — check your network connection.” with a Retry button.

ch19-delete.heading: Delete a project
steps: Open the project detail and expand the Danger zone section (collapsed by default). It appears only for leadership — leader, leading-division head, or admin.
Read the hint: “Can only be deleted when it has no meetings.”
Click Delete project (trash icon) and confirm “Delete project "{name}"? This cannot be undone.”.
On success the detail closes and a toast reads “Project "{name}" deleted.”
If the project still has meetings, the deletion is refused with the alert “Delete all meetings in the project before deleting it.” — use View meetings → to go clean them up first.
ch19-delete.outcome: A project can only be deleted once it's empty, so its meeting history is never silently destroyed. The action is permanent.
ch19-delete.note: A co-operator never sees the Danger zone — only true leadership (leader / head / admin) can delete. An invitee-only folder never shows it either.

host.html: Any other failure shows “Couldn't delete the project.” — usually a network blip; try again.

ch19-trouble.heading: Project administration fixes

rows.sym: No Manage projects item in the sidebar
rows.cause: You're signed in as a guest (external) account.
rows.fix: Project administration is internal-staff only. Sign in with your staff account.

rows.sym: Can see a project but no Edit / Add member buttons
rows.cause: You're a plain participant, or only invited into the folder for one meeting.
rows.fix: Ask the project leader or a co-operator to grant you a managing role. Invitee folders are always view-only.

rows.sym: Read-only banner on a project's detail
rows.cause: Another department invited you in for a single meeting.
rows.fix: “You're invited to this project — view only.” You can see it but not administer it; that's expected.

rows.sym: Can't make someone a co-operator
rows.cause: You're a co-operator, not leadership.
rows.fix: Only the leader, leading-division head or admin can delegate roles. Ask one of them.

rows.sym: Add member rejected
rows.cause: You tried to add a non-internal email.
rows.fix: “Couldn't add member (internal emails only).” Only staff accounts can be project members; issue a guest ID for external people instead.

rows.sym: Delete refused
rows.cause: The project still contains meetings.
rows.fix: “Delete all meetings in the project before deleting it.” Open View meetings →, remove them, then delete.

rows.sym: Project list empty slot says couldn't load
rows.cause: The list fetch failed (network / server).
rows.fix: “Couldn't load — check your network connection.” Click Retry; your existing list is kept, not blanked.

rows.sym: Extra details didn't save after create
rows.cause: The metadata save (second step) failed.
rows.fix: “Project created, but saving extra details failed — press Edit to retry.” Open Edit project and re-enter the rest.

ch19-trouble.note: Cosmetic colour/icon changes and member edits each refresh just the one item in place — the list never flashes. If an action seems to do nothing, check for a toast at the bottom of the screen; that's where these messages appear.

ch20-two-modes.heading: Two modes, one form
ch20-two-modes.lead: Create & join or Create & invite — the same panel serves both, and the only difference is whether the meeting starts now or sits on a date you choose.
ch20-two-modes.body:
When you press the project's New meeting button, the form opens in now mode: the meeting is created with status live and you are taken straight into the room the moment you submit. There is no date picker — a now-meeting starts the instant it is born.

When you open the form to Schedule — by clicking a day in the calendar column on the right — it opens in schedule mode. Now you get a date, a time, and a duration. The meeting is created with status scheduled; you are not taken into a room. Instead it appears in every invitee's Invited / Upcoming list, ready for its hour.

Everything else — title, agenda, roles, people — is identical between the two. The form deliberately mirrors the edit form: what you can set when you create a meeting is exactly what you can change later.

diagram.label: now vs. schedule
diagram.cap: The same panel, two lifecycles: now → live → you enter; schedule → scheduled → Upcoming list.

note.html: The New meeting and Schedule entry points only appear to project owners and co-operators. A plain participant browsing the project will not see them — they receive meetings through invitations, covered in the next chapter.

ch20-open-form.heading: Opening the form
steps: To start a meeting right now, open a project and press New meeting at the top of the meetings column. The form opens in now mode, bound to that project.
To plan one ahead, look at the calendar in the right-hand column and click the day you want. The form opens in schedule mode with that date pre-filled.
When you open Schedule from the calendar with no project selected, the top of the form shows a project Select a project dropdown — you must pick one before you can submit.
The title field is focused automatically, so you can begin typing the moment the panel appears.
Changed your mind? Press the back arrow in the top-left of the panel (its label is Leave) to close without creating anything.
ch20-open-form.outcome: The right-hand panel now shows the meeting form — a back arrow and a New meeting or Schedule heading at the top, four stacked zones below, and a single primary button at the foot.

host.html: If you manage several projects, the schedule-mode project dropdown lists every project you can create meetings in. The chosen project decides which guest list appears later — the form never silently files a meeting under an arbitrary project.

ch20-open-form.figcap: The four-zone meeting form: Essentials, Agenda, Roles & settings, People.

ch20-essentials.heading: Title, date, time, duration
steps: Type a Meeting title in the large field at the top. This is the only required field — the submit button stays disabled until it has text.
In schedule mode, set the Date & time. Click the date box to pop the native date picker; if the meeting is unscheduled you may leave the date blank.
Pick a start time from the dropdown — it offers every half-hour from midnight to 23:30. The time defaults to 09:00 (or the time you clicked in the calendar).
Set the Duration (min) in the number box; it defaults to 60 and steps in fives. The quiet min suffix sits beside it.
In now mode there is no date row at all — the meeting starts immediately, so date, time, and duration simply do not appear.
ch20-essentials.outcome: A titled meeting with, in schedule mode, a concrete start moment and length. Leaving the date empty in schedule mode creates the meeting with no scheduled time — it shows as Not scheduled and you can set a time later via Reschedule.
ch20-essentials.note: The time dropdown is click-only — there is no free-typing of arbitrary minutes. Choose the nearest half-hour, then fine-tune the meeting later if you need an odd start time.

ch20-agenda.heading: Topic, description, and the four vocabularies
rows: Placeholder “e.g. Façade review” — the meeting's one-line focus.
Placeholder “Add notes…” — longer agenda or context.
Design review · Kickoff · Coordination · Client presentation · Internal sync · QA-QC · Other
Architecture · Structure · MEP · Façade · Interior · Landscape · General
ch20-agenda.note: Every dropdown carries a blank — entry at the top, so each tag is optional — leave it blank and the meeting simply has no value for that field. The four vocabularies are the same set you see when editing a meeting or filtering the project list.

host.html: These tags are how a busy project stays legible: Confidentiality in particular signals whether external guests belong in the room. They are labels, not locks — set them honestly so co-operators reading the project list can tell a Confidential design review from a Client-shared presentation at a glance.

ch20-roles.heading: Naming the host and co-host
steps: Pick the Host from the dropdown. It defaults to you, the organizer — every internal person you have invited also appears as a candidate.
Optionally pick a Co-host. The dropdown opens on — None —; the list is the same internal candidates minus whoever is currently host.
Only internal invitees can host or co-host — guests never appear in these dropdowns. To make someone a host candidate, invite them in the People zone first.
If you choose a host who is already the co-host, the form clears the co-host automatically so the two roles can't collide.
Note the two switch rows — Waiting room for guests and Record the meeting. Both are labelled (coming soon) and are switched off and disabled; they are placeholders, not yet-enforced policies.
ch20-roles.outcome: The meeting carries a designated host (you by default) and, optionally, a pre-assigned co-host whose invitation arrives already stamped with the co-host role.
ch20-roles.note: If you invite someone, name them host, then remove them from the People list, the form keeps the now-orphaned name selectable rather than silently snapping back — so the host you chose never quietly changes underneath you.

host.html: Pre-naming a host matters most for meetings you schedule but won't run yourself. The named host can start the room in your place, and the usual host away → acting host fallback still applies if neither of you arrives.

ch20-people.heading: Inviting the room
steps: Search internal colleagues in the Search by name / department… box — it matches name, email, division, and job title — then click a result to add them.
Prefer a checklist? Press Members to open the Select members picker, tick everyone you need, and confirm with Done.
Invite external contacts from Project guests: search and click a name. Guests must already be issued in the guest manager — there is no free-typed email box here.
Each person you add appears in the grid at the top of the zone, clustered by division with their avatar; press the remove control to drop anyone.

When at least one internal person is selected, a checkbox Also grant project access (internal only) appears, ticked by default — leave it on to give colleagues standing access to the project, not just this one meeting.
ch20-people.outcome: On submit, everyone selected is invited to the meeting; the pre-named co-host's invite carries the co-host role, and ticked internal colleagues are added to the project.
ch20-people.note: The internal search shows the first 50 matches and the guest search the first 30; narrow your query if someone is missing. When a search finds nobody you'll see No one found (internal) or No project guests yet — issue one in the guest manager (guests).

host.html: The guest list is strictly per-project: only guests issued to this project appear, and they are invited by their project login, never a raw email. That is what keeps each department's external contacts walled off from the others.

ch20-submit.heading: Create & join, or Create & invite

tiles.cap: In now mode the foot button reads Create & join. Press it and the meeting is created live and you are taken straight into the room.
In schedule mode the button reads Create & invite. The meeting is created scheduled; you stay on the dashboard and it surfaces in everyone's Upcoming list.

ch20-submit.useWhen: The button is disabled until the title has text, and again while the create is in flight, so a double-press can't make two meetings. If the server refuses the create — a permissions or connection problem — the form stays open and shows Save failed — check your permission (organizer only) or the meeting state. rather than pretending it worked.

ch20-trouble.eyebrow: When it doesn't go to plan
ch20-trouble.heading: Scheduling troubleshooting

rows.sym: The create button is greyed out and won't click.
rows.cause: The Meeting title is empty, or a create is already running.
rows.fix: Type a title. The button enables the moment the title has non-blank text; if you just pressed it, wait for the in-flight create to finish.

rows.sym: In schedule mode from the calendar, I can't submit.
rows.cause: No project is bound — the form opened with no project context.
rows.fix: Pick a project in the Select a project dropdown at the top of the form, then submit.

rows.sym: Submitting shows “Save failed — check your permission…”.
rows.cause: The server refused the create — you're not the organizer for that action, or the worker is unreachable.
rows.fix: Confirm you own or co-operate the project and that you're online, then try again. The form keeps your entries.

rows.sym: A colleague I want as host isn't in the Host dropdown.
rows.cause: Only internal invitees are host candidates; the person isn't yet invited.
rows.fix: Add them in the People zone first — they then appear as a host and co-host candidate.

rows.sym: The Project guests list is empty.
rows.cause: This project has no guests issued, or your search matched none.
rows.fix: Clear the search; if it's still empty, issue a guest ID in the guest manager first — guests can't be free-typed here.

rows.sym: The Waiting room / Record switches won't turn on.
rows.cause: Both are marked (coming soon) and are intentionally disabled.
rows.fix: Nothing to do — they're placeholders for a future release, not active policies.

ch20-trouble.note: Leaving the date blank in schedule mode is not an error — the meeting is created with no scheduled time and shows as Not scheduled. Give it a time later with Reschedule.

ch21-model.heading: A guest is a contact, not an account
ch21-model.lead: A guest never signs in with their real email. Instead you issue a guest ID — the app mints a synthetic login and a temporary password that exist only for one project. You hand those credentials to the client; they use them to enter every meeting in that project, and nowhere else.
ch21-model.body: Guest access is independent per project. The hint above each issue form says it plainly: Issue a guest ID scoped to THIS project. The guest follows the project across every meeting. Each project is independent — other departments can't see it. A client invited into one project is invisible to every other project, which is how confidentiality between departments is kept. Around the synthetic login the app stores a contact card — representative name, real email, company, phone, address, country, and a company logo. Those are reference details only; they are never part of the sign-in identity.

note.html: The real email you record on the card is for your reference. The client signs in with the synthetic Login the app generates, never with their email — so the same person can be a guest of two projects under two unrelated logins, and neither project sees the other.

ch21-where.heading: Per-project, or the all-projects manager
ch21-where.lead: You can manage a project's guests from two places, and they share the same controls. Inside a project, open the project's detail page and expand the Project guests section; the Add guest shortcut next to Add member jumps you straight to its issue form. This view is scoped to that one project.
ch21-where.body: The second place is the centralised Guest manager — its own item in the left nav of the dashboard, labelled Guest manager, opening a page titled Guest manager (all projects). Here every guest you can manage is listed grouped by project, and a project picker at the top of the issue form lets you issue into any project you run without leaving the page. Its hint reads: Manage guests across the projects you run. Each project is independent — pick a project to issue a guest ID.

note.html: Issuing and managing guests is for the people who run a project — admin, leader, co-operator, or division head. A plain participant sees the project roster read-only with no Add guest shortcut, and an invitee never sees the guests section at all. The Guest manager nav item only appears for internal staff, and its list is scoped server-side to the projects you actually belong to.

legend.text: Page hint — Manage guests across the projects you run…
Project picker (Guest manager only) — choose which project to issue into; lists only projects you run.
Guest details grid — Representative, Email (optional), Company, Phone, Address, and the Country (picks backdrop) select.
Issue guest ID button — disabled until a project is chosen and Representative is filled.
Credentials panel — appears once after issuing, with Login, Password, and Copy login + password.
Guests grouped by project, each group headed by its name, a count, and a Retire all guests button.
A guest row — logo, name, company, country, login, contact lines, and the action buttons (logo, edit, reset, revoke).

ch21-fields.heading: Every field on a guest
rows: Which project the guest ID is scoped to. Only projects you run are listed; in the per-project view it's fixed.
The contact person's name. Shown as the guest's name; falls back to the login if left blank on an old record.
The client's real email, for your reference only. Never used to sign in.
Client's company; shown beside the name in the roster.
Reference contact number, shown on the guest row.
Reference address, shown on the guest row.
ISO country with flag; sets the client's entry-page backdrop. Empty = the global default backdrop.
image button on the guest row
Company logo thumbnail (set after issuing, see below).
ch21-fields.note: Email, company, phone, address, and country are all free-text reference fields stored next to the synthetic login — they are never part of the auth identity. Country is the one with a visible side-effect: it chooses the backdrop the client sees on their entry page.

host.html: You can't choose the guest's login name or password — both are generated. The Reset password action mints a fresh password but keeps the same login, so a returning client keeps their identity.

ch21-creds.heading: Copy the login + password (shown once)
steps: After issuing, read the Guest ID issued panel. It shows Login and Password on two lines.
Note the warning: Send this login + password to the guest. Shown only once — copy now.
Press Copy login + password. The button flips to Copied ✓ for two seconds.
Paste the credentials into your message to the client and send them on.
Move on — the panel does not reappear, and the password is never recoverable.
ch21-creds.outcome: The client now has a login and password that admit them to every meeting in this project. They enter on the client portal — no account, no email verification.
ch21-creds.note: The password is displayed only once. There is no "show again". If clipboard access is blocked, the copy action falls back to a prompt box you can copy from by hand, so you never lose the credentials. If you miss the copy, use Reset password later to mint and copy a fresh one — the login stays the same.

host.html: Don't email the password before you've copied it from this panel — once you issue the next guest or reload, the panel is gone. Reset password is your recovery path, and it produces the same Guest's new password panel with a fresh Copy login + password button.

ch21-card.heading: Edit details, reset, or revoke
steps: Find the guest in the list. Each row carries four action buttons on the right.
Press the pencil (Edit details) to open the card inline; change any field and press Save, or Cancel to drop the edit.
Press the key (Reset password) to mint a new password for the same login; the Guest's new password panel appears to copy.
Press the trash (Revoke) to cut off one guest; confirm the prompt to proceed.
Use Retire all guests in a project's group header to revoke every guest of that project at once.
ch21-card.outcome: Edits save immediately (toast Guest details saved). A reset gives the client a new password without changing who they are. A revoke removes their access while keeping their card and history.
ch21-card.note: Save stays disabled while Representative is blank — the name is required on edit too. Revoke asks: Revoke {label}'s access? They lose access — their details & history are KEPT (not deleted). Retire all guests asks: Revoke access for ALL guests of this project? They lose access — no data/history is deleted. and afterwards toasts Revoked {count} guests. Failures toast Couldn't save the guest's details., Couldn't reset the password., or Couldn't revoke the guest.

host.html: Revoking is reversible only by issuing a fresh guest ID — there is no "un-revoke". Because the card and history are kept, retiring guests at the end of a project is safe: you lose nobody's record, only their live access. In the per-project view the Retire all guests button sits at the bottom of the list; in the Guest manager it sits in each project group's header.

ch21-logo.heading: The three logo states

tiles.cap: A placeholder image icon shows in the row's logo slot. The action button reads Upload logo — press it to pick an image file.
The uploaded logo renders as a thumbnail. A second button appears — Remove logo (the X) — to clear it. The toast Logo saved confirms an upload.
With a logo already set, the upload button's tooltip becomes Replace logo. Picking a new image swaps it in place.

ch21-logo.useWhen: Add a logo when you want the client's brand to show on their guest row. Files must be images and are capped at 2 MB by the server; a non-image or oversize file toasts Couldn't save the logo (image up to 2MB).

ch21-lifecycle.heading: Guest actions at a glance
rows: Mints a synthetic login + one-time password scoped to the project; shows the credentials panel once.
Copies login / password to the clipboard (or a prompt box if blocked); button shows Copied ✓.
Opens the contact card inline; Save writes, Cancel discards. Never touches the login.
Mints a new password for the same login; shows the Guest's new password panel to copy.
Sets or swaps the company logo (image, up to 2 MB).
Clears the logo back to the placeholder.
Removes one guest's access; their card and history are kept.
Revokes every guest of one project at once; no data deleted.
ch21-lifecycle.note: Every action on a single guest is mutually exclusive while it runs — pressing one disables that row's other buttons until it finishes, so a reset and a revoke can't collide.

host.html: Edit, reset, upload, and remove never prompt — they apply at once. Only the two destructive actions (Revoke and Retire all guests) ask first, and both spell out that history is kept.

ch21-trouble.heading: Guest troubleshooting

rows.sym: Issue guest ID is greyed out
rows.cause: No project is selected, or Representative is blank (or only spaces).
rows.fix: Pick a project and type a real name; the button enables once both are set.

rows.sym: No Guest manager item in the dashboard nav
rows.cause: The all-projects manager is internal-staff only.
rows.fix: Use the per-project Project guests section instead, or ask an admin.

rows.sym: No Project guests section on a project page
rows.cause: You're a plain participant or invitee, who can't manage guests.
rows.fix: Only admin, leader, co-operator, or head see it. Ask the project's manager.

rows.sym: Project picker shows No guests across your projects yet. / no options
rows.cause: You don't run any project the manager can issue into.
rows.fix: Become a member/owner of a project first; invitee access can't issue guests.

rows.sym: I lost the password before sending it
rows.cause: Credentials show only once and aren't recoverable.
rows.fix: Press Reset password on the guest to mint and copy a fresh one; the login is unchanged.

rows.sym: Client can't sign in with their email
rows.cause: Guests sign in with the synthetic Login, not their email.
rows.fix: Send them the Login string from the credentials panel, not the email on the card.

rows.sym: Couldn't save the logo (image up to 2MB).
rows.cause: The file wasn't an image, or exceeded 2 MB.
rows.fix: Pick an image file under 2 MB (PNG, JPG, etc.).

rows.sym: Toast Couldn't issue the guest ID. / …revoke the guest.
rows.cause: The server rejected the request (network or permission).
rows.fix: Retry; if it persists confirm you still manage the project.

ch21-trouble.note: Revoking and retiring keep every guest's contact card and meeting history — they only remove live access. There is no permanent delete of a guest's record from these screens.

ch22-lifecycle.heading: A meeting moves through four states — and only actions move it
ch22-lifecycle.lead: A meeting is never edited into a new state; it is acted into one. Canvas M tracks exactly four canonical statuses — Scheduled, Live, Finished and Cancelled — and each transition has its own button. There is no status dropdown anywhere in the editor, by design.
ch22-lifecycle.body: Scheduled → Live happens when someone with start rights presses Start meeting. Live → Finished happens when a host presses End meeting (the red power button). Scheduled → Cancelled happens from the meeting's detail panel via Cancel meeting. The one way back out of cancelled is Restore meeting, which returns it to Scheduled; a cancelled meeting can also be disposed of permanently with Delete forever. Finished is immutable — you cannot edit, reschedule, or reopen it as live again; reopening a finished room lands everyone in read-only review.
ch22-lifecycle.pull: Finished is the one-way door. End the meeting only when you mean it.

diagram.label: Status flow: Scheduled ↔ Cancelled, Scheduled → Live → Finished
diagram.cap: The server enforces the same transitions the buttons offer — there is no other path between states.

note.html: Lifecycle controls appear for the organizer, the meeting host, a designated co-host, or a project authority (division head / project leader). Everyone else sees the meeting but none of the management buttons — the worker re-checks the same rule, so a hidden button is also a blocked request.

ch22-start.heading: Starting a scheduled meeting
steps: Open the meeting link or pick the meeting from your project. If it is still Scheduled, the full-screen start gate appears with the meeting title and, when set, Scheduled for ….
If you belong to the owning department, you see a Start meeting button. Press it. While it works the label reads Starting….

If you are not allowed to start (a cross-department invitee), you instead see a spinner and Waiting for the host to start the meeting… — the gate polls every five seconds and drops you straight into the room the instant any host starts it.
Once live, you land in the meeting shell: canvas in the centre, the header across the top, the people strip along the bottom.
ch22-start.outcome: The meeting flips to Live in the registry, which is what releases every other person still waiting on the gate. Your own join is identical to any other live join.

host.html: The Start meeting button is gated by the server-computed owning-department scope (organizer / host / co-host / project authority / same-division member). A guest or outside invitee never sees it — they wait. If the meeting was cancelled or finished while you were parked on the gate, pressing Start re-reads the truth and routes you to the cancelled notice or read-only review instead of barging in.

ch22-start.figcap: The start gate, before the host presses Start.

legend.text: Project · meeting title — click to edit name / topic / metadata (organizer-only; a ⌄ chevron shows when editable). Tooltip: Click to edit meeting name / topic.
Meeting clock — an objective timer counting from when the host started, so late joiners see the same elapsed time. Tooltip: Meeting time elapsed.
People count — reads joined / invited; click to open the Participants panel. A small mic sub-badge shows how many are in the audio call.
Media group — mic, camera and leave-call (from the call controls) framed with Present (screen share). Present locks while someone else is sharing.
Captions (CC) and Transcript — toggle live captions from any view; the transcript icon carries a count badge of logged segments.
Meeting group — layout switcher, Invite (accent, organizer/host/co-host only), and Projects (host-only folder).
End meeting — the red Power button at the far right. Host / co-host / organizer / authority only. Ends the room for everyone.

ch22-invite.heading: Inviting colleagues and project guests
steps: In the header's Meeting group, press the accent Invite button (a person-plus icon). The Invite people panel slides in.
Pick Internal colleagues from the staff directory — type in Search by name / department… and click a name to add a chip. Each pick shows their title and division.

Add this project's issued guests from the second list (search field placeholder below the Briefcase label). Guests must already be issued in the project — there is no free-typed external email here, by design (per-department confidentiality).

When at least one internal person is selected, the Also grant project access (internal only) checkbox appears (on by default) — leave it on to give them whole-folder access, not just this one meeting.
Press Grant access (the button shows a live count, e.g. Grant access (3)). On success it reads Access granted ✓ — remember to send guests the link and copies the room link to your clipboard.
ch22-invite.outcome: Invitees get an access grant (a login plus a meeting_invitee row). There are no automatic invite emails — Canvas M deliberately does not share by raw room URL, so paste the copied link to the people you just granted. Use Copy invite link at the top of the panel any time to grab it again.

host.html: Invite is visible only to the organizer, host, co-host, or project authority, and only while the meeting still takes edits — it disappears in a finished meeting and in read-only review. If the worker refuses, the panel shows the exact reason: You don't have permission to invite people to this meeting. (403) or The meeting has ended or was cancelled — no more invites. (409).

ch22-invite.figcap: The Invite people panel with internal and guest pickers.

ch22-waiting.heading: Letting guests in — admit or deny
steps: External guests who join a live meeting they haven't been admitted to are parked in a waiting room — they see Waiting to be let in and Waiting for the host to let you in…. Internal staff auto-admit and never appear here.
On your side, open the Participants panel (click the people count). When guests are knocking, the people strip shows an N waiting badge and the panel grows a Waiting to join (N) section.
For each knocker, press Admit (a check icon) to let them in, or Deny (red) to refuse. The row drops immediately; a failed call re-fetches so a knock is never silently lost.

A denied guest sees Not admitted with The host hasn't let you in right now. You can knock again in a moment. and a Knock again button — the re-knock is rate-limited to once every 30 seconds, server-side.
ch22-waiting.outcome: Admitted guests connect immediately, entering muted (the room starts with audio off). If you end the meeting while a guest is mid-admit, their client re-reads the meeting and quietly backs out rather than barging into a finished room.

host.html: The knock list polls every five seconds and is gated on server-confirmed authority, not the local acting-host election — so only the organizer / host / co-host / project authority ever sees people waiting. A plain internal participant, even one the room briefly elected as acting host, sees no waiting section.

ch22-waiting.figcap: The Waiting to join section with Admit / Deny per guest.

ch22-moderate.heading: Who can mute, remove, and end

tiles.cap: The host (and a project authority) sees per-person Mute / Unmute and Remove on every other tile — both as hover buttons on the avatar strip and as full buttons in the Participants panel. The mute button reads the real broadcast state, so it offers Unmute when the person is already muted. A removed person sees The host removed you from the meeting.

A designated co-host carries a half-crown Co-host badge and can End meeting for everyone. In-room kick/mute follow the acting-host rule; the co-host role specifically authorises ending and inviting, which a random participant cannot do.

A project-scoped guest is never a moderator. Even if the socket host-election momentarily lands on them, mute / remove / end stay hidden — and the worker also refuses the host command server-side. Guests keep leave, transcript, present, and their own profile.

ch22-moderate.useWhen: Reach for moderation when a line is open and feeding back (mute), when someone joined the wrong room (remove), or to hand the ending to a co-host. The crown badge over an avatar always tells the room who is host without anyone having to ask.

ch22-end.heading: Ending the meeting for everyone
steps: Press the red End meeting (Power) button at the far right of the header. Confirm the prompt: End the meeting for EVERYONE? All participants switch to read-only review.

Canvas M marks the meeting Finished in the registry first. If that write fails it aborts and toasts Couldn't end the meeting — check your network and try again. — nothing changes, so you can simply retry.
On success, an AI recap is generated in the background from the transcript and chat (never blocking the ending) and stored on the meeting as its AI summary.
Everyone in the room is broadcast into read-only review, your own resume pointer is cleared so the meeting is never offered for resume again, and your own view switches to review.
ch22-end.outcome: The meeting is now Finished and immutable. Reopening it lands in review showing the banner Reviewing (read-only) · meeting finished — extract only. The auto-recap appears as a clamped AI summary card in the meeting's detail panel, with Show more / Show less for long recaps.

host.html: End is gated by designated role, not the socket election: only the host, co-host, organizer, or a division head / project leader sees the button. If nothing was said or typed, no recap is generated — the summary card simply stays absent. Generation is fire-and-forget, so a model hiccup never delays the meeting ending.

ch22-reschedule.heading: Reschedule, cancel, restore, delete
rows: Status is Scheduled and you can manage it

Reveals date / time (30-min slots) / duration fields; saving writes the new schedule. Save is disabled until a date is chosen. Once a meeting is Live the time can no longer change (Meeting has started — date & time can no longer change.).
Status is Scheduled and you can manage it
Confirms Cancel this meeting? Invitees will see it as cancelled. then moves it to Cancelled; invitees see the cancelled notice.
Status is Cancelled and you can manage it
Returns the meeting to Scheduled — the one transition the server allows out of cancelled.
Status is Cancelled and you can manage it
Confirms PERMANENTLY delete this meeting? Canvas, files and all history will be erased — this cannot be undone. then removes it and closes the panel. Canvas, files and every related row cascade away.
You can manage it and the meeting still takes edits (Scheduled or Live)
Opens the metadata editor for title, topic, agenda and fields. Finished is immutable; a cancelled meeting must be restored first.
ch22-reschedule.note: Open these from the meeting's detail panel: select the meeting in your project to load its hero card, where the lifecycle buttons sit beneath the schedule line.

host.html: All five actions are organizer / authority gated and disabled while a save is in flight. A refused save surfaces Save failed — check your permission (organizer only) or the meeting state.

ch22-trouble.heading: Host troubleshooting

rows.sym: No Start meeting button on the gate
rows.cause: You are not in the owning department — only organizer / host / co-host / authority / same-division members may start.
rows.fix: Wait for the spinner Waiting for the host to start the meeting…; the gate auto-joins you the instant a host starts. Or ask the organizer to start.

rows.sym: Invite button is missing from the header
rows.cause: You are a plain participant or guest, or the meeting has finished / is in read-only review.
rows.fix: Inviting needs organizer / host / co-host / authority on a still-editable meeting. A finished meeting can't be invited into.

rows.sym: Guest stuck — no Waiting to join section appears for you
rows.cause: The knock poll runs only for server-confirmed authority; an acting-host who isn't the organizer doesn't see knocks.
rows.fix: Have the organizer, host, co-host or division head open the Participants panel to admit. Guests can press Knock again after the 30s cooldown.

rows.sym: Mute / Remove not on a participant's tile
rows.cause: You aren't the host / authority, or the tile is yourself or the host (you can't moderate those).
rows.fix: Moderation appears only on OTHER participants and only for the host or a project authority.

rows.sym: Ending the meeting toasts a failure
rows.cause: The registry write to mark it Finished didn't go through (network).
rows.fix: Couldn't end the meeting — check your network and try again. Nothing changed — press End meeting again.

rows.sym: No AI summary card after a meeting
rows.cause: Nothing was said or typed, so there was no transcript or chat to recap; or the summariser hiccuped (non-blocking).
rows.fix: Expected when a meeting had no audio or chat. Recaps are best-effort and never block ending — the card simply stays absent.

rows.sym: Can't change the date — fields say it's locked
rows.cause: The meeting is already Live; only Scheduled meetings can be rescheduled.
rows.fix: Meeting has started — date & time can no longer change. Reschedule before starting, or end and create a new one.

ch22-trouble.note: Most hidden host controls are also blocked at the server, so a missing button is a real permission boundary, not a UI glitch — check your role first.
